Then turn around and open the gate, that has been previously locked. Use the elevator down and meet a Darkwraith in a room full of corpses. He carries a sword and a Dark Hand . The dark hand is a shieldlike object, that can block and use a life draining grapple. Dodge, once his left hand starts glowing white. Unlike the Lothric Knights, these are much more aggressive. On death it will drop a Red Eye Orb , that has infinite uses for invasions. Return to Leonhard at Firelink Shrine to get the Applause Gesture. Irina of Carim With the Grave Key in your pocket, head to the Dilapidated Bridge Bonfire. Go over the wooden bridge into the sewers. Kill the three rats and head for the locked gate. With the key it can be opened. Turn right at the crossing and pick up the Loincloth . The statue can be used to absolve for sins (e.g. if you attacked the Shrine Handmaiden) or revert the hollowing points back to zero. Turn around and follow the path. Pick up the Red Hilted Halberd . Proceed into the next room and some skeletons will animate. Proceed slowly and don't trigger too many skeletons at the same time. In the next narrow room two skeletons will animate, one of them behind you. Don't forget the Soul of an Unknown Traveler and leave to the open. Go right and deal with the Crystal Lizard. Push him into the right wall to have an easier time. As you approach the two items, one giant hollow will drop down and ambush you. Kill him, pick up the two seperate Titanite Shards . Get back and proceed into the direction of the tower. There will be an entrance to your left and a corpse hanging from a beam. Shoot it down with an arrow to aquire the Blessed Red and White Shield +1 . Equipping this shield will give you a small HP regeneration. Go inside and prepare for a rat ambush. After the one visible, many more will crawl of that hole, which is quite dangerous. Loot the Saint's Talisman and head up the other ladder. To your left will be Irina of Carim. Exhaust her dialogue, choose "Touch" and accept her offer and she will head out for Firelink Shrine. She will be your merchant for miracles. Go into the other direction and open the gate. Talk to him and he agrees to join your cause.

sections.title: Boss: Curse-Rotted Greatwood
sections.content_html:
This boss is optional, but must be killed, if you want to transpose Boss Souls into weapons. Sorcerers might want to skip the boss and return later, once they have aquired the Pestilent Mercury sorcery.

The fastest way to the Boss is from the Cliff Underside Bonfire. Head up and drop down behind the giant hollow with the pot. Run upstairs and go into the arena. The boss is on the far left side and has a lot of undead villagers around. Once you get too close or attack the red-eyed undead on the right side, you trigger the bossfight.

Attacks

While you stand in front of the boss, he will occationally swipe with an arm and kill every undead standing there. It won't kill you outright, but deals much damage. Alternatively he can stomp or slamming both fists into the ground. All those are very well telegraphed and can be easily dodged. If you stand next to, or behind the enemy he will start shaking and dropping hurting spores. It's hard to avoid them, but its easier to stay away from him during this phase. He can also stand up and slam his bottom into the ground, which creates many yellow puddles, that hurt to stand in. Once they disappear, they change the pattern before they disappear. If you stand behind him, he might also lean back and squash everything under him.

During Phase 2 of the fight he will grow an additional hand. It has some quick swipes and a really painful grapple attack. It acts quicker, than the rest of the Greatwood.

Killing the Greatwood

The only way to hurt him is to destroy the white egg sacks in his crotch area. Those are also suspectible to fire damage. Once the sack is destroyed the Greatwood will slam again into the ground and destroy the arena. The drop is harmless to you but will kill the surrounding undead. It will then spawn another hand and several more egg sacks show up.

One is at his right leg, one at the left hand and back of the left leg, one at the back and a large one near the hand above the crotch. The one in the back can only be destroyed by ranged weapons or when it leans back a bit to bring it closer for melee characters. Destroying all sacks is enough to kill it off completly. Alternatively you can attack the second hand to deplete his HP.

If you are a sorcerer and have the Pestilent Mist from a later area, this fight becomes laughably easy. Simply cast the mist and stay away for as long as it lasts. This will damage the Greatwood without triggering Phase 2 of the fight.

Victory

Once it is dead, light the bonfire and head back to the Cliff Underside Bonfire. It drops the Transposing Kiln, that you can give to Ludleth back at Firelink Shrine. He is sitting on his throne.

sections.title: Wrapping up and Leaving
sections.content_html:
If you haven't looted the Flame Stoneplate Ring yet, you can do it now. Remember, that you can't reload the area before picking it up. After that, head for the tower, where you met Siegward. Use the elevator to get down to the basement.

The Outrider Knight

Send the elevator back up without going up yourself and follow the path. In the next room a tough enemy awaits you. Leave the item be for now and focus on the fight. You can run past him to the door and open it. Head through and light the Bonfire. You don't need to kill the Outrider Knight, but he drops a good weapon. His attacks inflict frostbite and are in a rhythm quite similar to those of Vordt.

You can also lure him back to the elevator and have him charge into the elevator shaft. Or you can stand outside the door (he won't follow through) and attack him with ranged weapons, wearing him down. Don't forget to loot the Ember next to him and leave for the Road of Sacrifice Bonfire.

sections.title: Overview
sections.content_html:
Overview


“

Take on the deadliest planet in the known galaxy as a team of dwarven mercenary miners in our upcoming procedurally generated co-op sci-fi shooter - Deep Rock Galactic!

In the far future, space mining is big business.

The interplanetary mining corporation DEEP ROCK GALACTIC specializes in securing the most dangerous dig sites in the galaxy. When they need a team for the toughest missions, they call in the Dwarves - mercenary miners, legendary for their ability to survive underground, and infamous for their brutality in combat.

Join a team of up to 4 players to fight, dig and explore your way through enormous cave systems, uncover the greatest riches, and make it out alive.

— from the official site

sections.title: Key Features
sections.content_html:
• 1-4 PLAYER CO-OP
    • Work together as a team to dig, explore, and fight your way through a massive cave system filled with hordes of deadly enemies and valuable resources. You will need to rely on your teammates if you want to survive the most hostile cave systems in the galaxy!
  • 4 UNIQUE CLASSES
    • Pick the right class for the job. Mow through enemies as the Gunner, scout ahead and light up the caves as the Scout, chew through solid rock as the Driller, or support the team with defensive structures and turrets as the Engineer.
  • FULLY DESTRUCTIBLE ENVIRONMENTS
    • Destroy everything around you to reach your goal. There is no set path so you can complete your mission your way. Drill straight down to your objective or build an intricate network of paths to explore your surroundings -- the choice is yours. But proceed with caution, you don’t want to stumble into an alien swarm unprepared!
  • PROCEDURALLY GENERATED CAVE NETWORK
    • Explore a network of procedurally generated cave systems filled with enemies to fight and riches to collect. There’s always something new to discover and no two playthroughs are alike.
  • HIGH-TECH GADGETS AND WEAPONS
    • Dwarves know what they need to bring to get the job done. This means the most powerful weapons and the most advanced gadgets around - flamethrowers, gatling guns, portable platform launchers, and much, much more.
  • LIGHT YOUR PATH
    • The underground caves are dark and full of terrors. You will need to bring your own lights if you want to illuminate these pitch-black caverns.

sections.title: Description
sections.content_html:
Deep Rock Galactic is a procedurally generated first person co-op shooter for up to 4 players, developed in Unreal Engine 4 by Ghost Ship Games, It was released into early access on Steam on the 28th February 2018, and launched to version 1.0 on the 13th of May 2020.

Players take on the role of a team of veteran dwarven space miners, venturing into the deepest, most dangerous cave systems of the most hostile planet ever discovered, to gather ores for their corporate overlords, while expanding their roster of class-based skills and unlocking new gear and weapons.

sections.title: Lore
sections.content_html:
A letter from Management

Congratulations, [NEW DWARVEN EMPLOYEE]! By signing up with DEEP ROCK GALACTIC, you have just taken your first step towards becoming an essential gear in the machine of the MOST TENACIOUS space mining corporation in the known galaxy!

At DEEP ROCK GALACTIC, we pride ourselves on having established practical dominance of some the most lucrative systems in the OUTER RIM.
While our foolish and cowardly competitors generally regard these as too volatile or high-risk, DEEP ROCK GALACTIC calls them home.

At this time, we have a total of 89 ORBITAL SPACE RIGS in operation throughout MORE THAN A DOZEN Outer Rim systems, with 16 MORE currently under construction.

However, a NEW MANDATE is upon us! While our digs number in the dozens already, we are currently engaged in our most daring and heavily orchestrated mining operation to date: The COMPLETE SUBJUGATION of the planet HOXXES IV.

HOXXES IV constitutes, to the best of our knowledge, the SINGLE MOST LUCRATIVE mining location in the galaxy, containing the RICHEST AND MOST DENSE concentrations of valuable minerals we have ever encountered.
However, it also just happens to be the SINGLE MOST HOSTILE place we have ever mapped. Several competitors before us have tried to tame Hoxxes IV, WITHOUT LUCK.

DEEP ROCK GALACTIC will succeed. DEEP ROCK GALACTIC is not in the business of failing.

MANAGEMENT BIDS YOU WELCOME, NEW MINER. WELCOME ABOARD.

Working at Deep Rock Galactic

TEAMWORK IS KEY
At DEEP ROCK GALACTIC we value TEAMWORK above all else! The sheer hostility of Hoxxes IV means anyone caught away from their team will be in for a world of hurt.
As a responsible INTERPLANETARY MINING CONGLOMERATE, we depend on our employees to take care of each other. In other words - we won’t be there holding your hand.

As the saying goes: "Dig together - or dig your own grave".

NEXT-LEVEL SPACE MINING
At DEEP ROCK GALACTIC we specialise in SPACE MINING at the most dangerous dig sites in the galaxy, and we call upon those with a natural predisposition towards hard, honest work!

We believe in LEAN MINING, and we expect the same of you. Why send in a massive and costly mining operation when a CRACK SQUAD of highly-skilled mining operatives will do?

MYSTERIOUS CAVES
At DEEP ROCK GALACTIC we say that any cave can be conquered, so long as our drills remain fueled and lubricated!

While no two caves will ever be the same, our dedicated RESEARCH DEPARTMENT is constantly at work peeling apart the tectonic layers of the planet, locating the most lucrative caves and categorizing them accordingly.

MOVE UP THE COMPANY LADDER
At DEEP ROCK GALACTIC we are big on PROMOTIONS! So big, in fact, that we tally up EVERYTHING you do and calculate your Rank based on that!

Upon first joining us, your Rank will be 0 (lovingly referred to as Greenbeards among the employees). You will not remain a Greenbeard for long, however - while your objectives will carry you ever further down, your standing within the company will only go up!*

*Provided, of course, you are fortunate and skilled enough to survive.

sections.title: Game support
sections.content_html:
Deep Rock Galactic Wiki is focused on creating the definitive guide to Deep Rock Galactic. But while we make an effort to be complete, which may include game bugs and fixes for them, we are not an official game support channel.

For official game support, the developers or members of the community can be contacted on the official Deep Rock Galactic Discord server if you need support.

Bugs and issues can be reported on the official BetaHub platform.

sections.title: Plot
sections.content_html:
While Aiba is hanging out in a chatroom, a hacker infiltrates it and leaves a message telling the members within to log into Cyberspace EDEN, a popular physical-interaction cyberspace network, to receive a "wonderful present". Although most of the room members declare it to be too suspicious to involve in, Aiba, along with users "Akkino" and "Blue Box" decide to look into it. Aiba meets them the next day as arranged in Kowloon, a hacker-infested area of EDEN, where they introduce themselves as Nokia Shiramine and Arata Sanada; shortly after, the three of them are given the "Digimon Capture" by the unknown hacker and locked into Kowloon. While searching for an exit, Aiba runs into a hacker named Yuugo, the leader of hacker team Zaxon who resembles a rumored "white boy ghost" said to have been sighted around EDEN, who teaches them how to use their Digimon Capture and reveals that Arata is in fact a skilled hacker. Shortly afterwards, Aiba, Nokia, and Arata run into a mysterious creature that attacks them, and although Arata manages to hack open a way out for them, the creature grabs onto Aiba's leg and corrupts their logout process.

Aiba emerges in the real world as a half-digitized entity and is rescued by a detective named Kyoko Kuremi, who specializes in cyber crimes and offers to take them into her service as her assistant. Aiba manifests an ability called Connect Jump, which allows them to travel into and through networks.

The game thereafter splits into three different simultaneous plotlines:

  • Aiba helps Nokia reunite with an Agumon and Gabumon she'd met and bonded with in Kowloon; she learns from them that Digimon are not hacker programs (as the public believes them to be) but living beings that come from a "Digital World", and that Agumon and Gabumon came to EDEN for a specific purpose that they can't remember. Nokia vows to help them recover their memories, but soon after begins to flee from confrontations with dangerous hackers; after being soundly defeated by Zaxon team hacker Fei Wong Tomoe Ignacio, she decides to become stronger and form her own hacker group, the Rebels, for the sake of improving relations between humans and Digimon. Her hard work allows Agumon and Gabumon to digivolve into WarGreymon and MetalGarurumon and sheer positivity ends up gaining her a large number of followers, causing Yuugo to worry that she might interfere with his goals of protecting EDEN and its hackers.
  • Arata, who remains evasive about his own past as a hacker, assists Aiba in investigating "Digital Shift" phenomena around Tokyo, in which areas become mysteriously half-digitized. They meet a scientist named Akemi Suedou who identifies the mysterious creature as an "Eater", a corrupted mass of data that is responsible for digitizing areas and causing human victims to fall into a comatose state called "EDEN Syndrome" by "eating" its mental data. Further encounters with Eater signify that it has links to the "white boy ghost" that keeps appearing around it, and that by "eating" data it can evolve into different forms. After Arata learns the truth about Aiba's condition and witnesses a number of acquaintances become victims of EDEN Syndrome, he resolves to do whatever he can to save them.
  • Yuuko Kamishiro, the daughter of the former president of Kamishiro Enterprises (the company that manages EDEN), requests Kyoko's detective agency to investigate her father's purported suicide and assists them in infiltrating the company when needed. Investigations via hacking into Kamishiro Enterprises areas reveal that the company's current president, Rie Kishibe, is planning a large EDEN update that ties into something called the "Paradise Lost Plan". Along the way, Aiba learns that Yuuko's older brother is in fact a victim of EDEN Syndrome.

Eventually, Yuugo mobilizes hackers around EDEN to attempt a large-scale hacking on Kamishiro Enterprises's high-security Valhalla Server for an unclear purpose. Arata attempts to intervene, revealing that he was in fact the leader of a top-class hacker group named Jude that dissolved due to a traumatic event that occurred during a previous Valhalla Server hacking attempt. Nokia, during a moment of determination, accidentally causes WarGreymon and MetalGarurumon to DNA Digivolve into Omnimon, but everything is quickly brought to a halt when Rie arrives and unleashes a large crowd of Eaters on the hackers, revealing that the entire setup was a trap to get Yuugo to accumulate Eater prey. While Omnimon puts a stop to the Eater rampage, Rie forcibly logs out Yuugo, who turns out to in actuality be Yuuko using a false EDEN avatar modeled after her older brother. Rie informs Yuuko that she'd imbued the avatar with an artificial personality that she had used to manipulate Yuko's actions, and begins a process of extracting Yuuko's memories.

Omnimon's restoration to his form causes him to remember that his true purpose of coming to EDEN was to save the Digital World from an infestation of Eaters, which were created from negative human emotions taking form in EDEN. The Digital World's ruler, King Drasil, had determined that humans were the cause, and its Royal Knights were split in deciding whether or not its will was to destroy humanity to eradicate the Eaters. Deducing that Rie's plan is to open a dimensional door to allow the Royal Knights in, Aiba and their friends chase after her in order to stop her and save Yuuko, but due to the interference of Suedou, who reveals that he was the one who had handed out the Digimon Capture, they fail to stop her from opening the gate and revealing herself to be the Royal Knight Crusadermon. The group then attempts to save Yuuko, who has been absorbed by Eater into an entity called Eater Eve, but even after defeating it Yuuko refuses to emerge from her despair at being manipulated. Aiba, realizing that Eater is digital and they can Connect Jump into it. With the help of Fei's TigerVespamon, they convince Yuuko that she's not alone and get her out, but Aiba is pulled into a digital void; there, they meet the real Yuugo Kamishiro, Yuuko's brother and a victim of Eater. He wishes Aiba and their friends well before asking them not to search for him and a mysterious Digimon rescues them.

Aiba returns to the real world to discover that weeks have passed and the opened dimensional portal has caused the entire world to become a giant Digital Shift and that Digimon are running amok in the real world. The group begins to search for the other Royal Knights in the hopes of convincing them to join their sides instead of trying to destroy humanity. In the process, Aiba and Yuuko discover from Makoto Yamashina, a former member of Kamishiro Enterprises, that eight years prior there had been an EDEN beta test eight years prior involving five children; one of them, Yuugo, had become the first EDEN Syndrome victim, while the other four had their memories of the incident wiped by Suedou and the incident was covered up. Shortly after, Suedou sparks a certain memory back in Arata, which causes him to gain an obsession with becoming stronger and leave with him.

Aiba and their friends eventually manage to recruit most of the Royal Knights through various means; in the meantime, Arata partially merges with Eater and begins to rampage around town by "eating" data. A confrontation reveals that Crusadermon was in fact responsible for the murder of Yuuko's father, and that the five children from the EDEN beta test were in fact none other than Yuugo, Yuuko, Arata, Nokia, and Aiba, sending them into a recreation of the events of how they found a hole in EDEN, made first contact with the Digital World, and accidentally led Eater into it, thus accidentally instigating the Eater infestation. In order to save them as Crusadermon attacks, Kyoko arrives and reveals her true form as Alphamon, the thirteenth Royal Knight; after Crusadermon's defeat, Kyoko reveals that she and Rie are in fact former humans whose minds were victims of Eater and had their bodies possessed by Alphamon and Crusadermon, and that their own personalities have received slight influences from their human mediums.

As Aiba and company head to the Tokyo Metropolitan Office to stop Leopardmon, the leader of the Royal Knights' human genocide plan, Arata, mired completely despair over having let Yuugo become an Eater victim and forgotten his own best friend, transforms completely into an Eater, but Aiba manages to save him with Connect Jump in the same way they saved Yuuko. After stopping Leopardmon, Suedou tells the group that they can stop Eater by travelling to its core in the Digital World and extracting Yuugo from it, which will make it so that Eater and EDEN Syndrome never existed. The group arrives to find King Drasil having been taken over completely by Eater into an entity called the Mother Eater; after defeating it, Aiba Connect Jumps in and extracts Yuugo, who refuses to be saved and reveals that, because he had been acting as a limiter on Eater's actions, without him as a central conscience it has no restraint to simply eat everything indiscriminately.

Suedou takes the opportunity to merge with Mother Eater and become its new conscience, hoping to recreate the world and make it evolve into a world without misery, forcing the others to band together and defeat him. Despite knowing that continually Connect Jumping into Eater will take a toll on their body, Aiba does so anyway in the hopes of rescuing Suedou. Suedou, amazed that Aiba would attempt to save someone like him and claiming that such a thing is outside King Drasil's calculations, decides to have faith that the future isn't fated to end in sadness and sends Aiba away so that he can reboot King Drasil and disappear with Eater.

As Aiba returns to their friends and watches the reforming Digital World, King Drasil performs a restoration on it, meaning that the humans will have to return to their own world, the Digital World will be returned to the state it was in eight years prior, and the world will be reverted to a state in which contact with the Digimon never happened. Alphamon and the other Digimon bid farewell under the promise to meet again, and Aiba accompanies their friends back to the human world, but on the way back they dissolve into data before their friends' eyes.

In the real world, with its status changed so that Digimon contact never happened, only Nokia, Arata, Yuugo, and Yuuko remember the events while Aiba is still comatose; Yuuko's father is alive again, while Rie is a normal human woman, and Suedou was made to have never been born. Eventually, Aiba's scrap data is found by Alphamon, who has their Digimon team gather data from their memories of them to recreate their mind and restore them to their body. After being restored, Aiba meets Kyoko, who has no memory of the incident or of them, but invites them to work as her assistant.
sections.content_text: Logo While Aiba is hanging out in a chatroom, a hacker infiltrates it and leaves a message telling the members within to log into Cyberspace EDEN , a popular physical-interaction cyberspace network, to receive a "wonderful present". Although most of the room members declare it to be too suspicious to involve in, Aiba, along with users "Akkino" and "Blue Box" decide to look into it. Aiba meets them the next day as arranged in Kowloon, a hacker-infested area of EDEN, where they introduce themselves as Nokia Shiramine and Arata Sanada ; shortly after, the three of them are given the "Digimon Capture" by the unknown hacker and locked into Kowloon. While searching for an exit, Aiba runs into a hacker named Yuugo , the leader of hacker team Zaxon who resembles a rumored "white boy ghost" said to have been sighted around EDEN, who teaches them how to use their Digimon Capture and reveals that Arata is in fact a skilled hacker. Shortly afterwards, Aiba, Nokia, and Arata run into a mysterious creature that attacks them, and although Arata manages to hack open a way out for them, the creature grabs onto Aiba's leg and corrupts their logout process. Aiba emerges in the real world as a half-digitized entity and is rescued by a detective named Kyoko Kuremi , who specializes in cyber crimes and offers to take them into her service as her assistant. Aiba manifests an ability called Connect Jump, which allows them to travel into and through networks. The game thereafter splits into three different simultaneous plotlines: Aiba helps Nokia reunite with an Agumon and Gabumon she'd met and bonded with in Kowloon; she learns from them that Digimon are not hacker programs (as the public believes them to be) but living beings that come from a "Digital World", and that Agumon and Gabumon came to EDEN for a specific purpose that they can't remember. Nokia vows to help them recover their memories, but soon after begins to flee from confrontations with dangerous hackers; after being soundly defeated by Zaxon team hacker Fei Wong Tomoe Ignacio , she decides to become stronger and form her own hacker group, the Rebels , for the sake of improving relations between humans and Digimon. Her hard work allows Agumon and Gabumon to digivolve into WarGreymon and MetalGarurumon and sheer positivity ends up gaining her a large number of followers, causing Yuugo to worry that she might interfere with his goals of protecting EDEN and its hackers. Arata, who remains evasive about his own past as a hacker, assists Aiba in investigating "Digital Shift" phenomena around Tokyo, in which areas become mysteriously half-digitized. They meet a scientist named Akemi Suedou who identifies the mysterious creature as an " Eater ", a corrupted mass of data that is responsible for digitizing areas and causing human victims to fall into a comatose state called " EDEN Syndrome " by "eating" its mental data. Further encounters with Eater signify that it has links to the "white boy ghost" that keeps appearing around it, and that by "eating" data it can evolve into different forms. After Arata learns the truth about Aiba's condition and witnesses a number of acquaintances become victims of EDEN Syndrome, he resolves to do whatever he can to save them. Yuuko Kamishiro , the daughter of the former president of Kamishiro Enterprises (the company that manages EDEN), requests Kyoko's detective agency to investigate her father's purported suicide and assists them in infiltrating the company when needed. Investigations via hacking into Kamishiro Enterprises areas reveal that the company's current president, Rie Kishibe , is planning a large EDEN update that ties into something called the "Paradise Lost Plan". Along the way, Aiba learns that Yuuko's older brother is in fact a victim of EDEN Syndrome. Eventually, Yuugo mobilizes hackers around EDEN to attempt a large-scale hacking on Kamishiro Enterprises's high-security Valhalla Server for an unclear purpose. Arata attempts to intervene, revealing that he was in fact the leader of a top-class hacker group named Jude that dissolved due to a traumatic event that occurred during a previous Valhalla Server hacking attempt. Nokia, during a moment of determination, accidentally causes WarGreymon and MetalGarurumon to DNA Digivolve into Omnimon, but everything is quickly brought to a halt when Rie arrives and unleashes a large crowd of Eaters on the hackers, revealing that the entire setup was a trap to get Yuugo to accumulate Eater prey. While Omnimon puts a stop to the Eater rampage, Rie forcibly logs out Yuugo, who turns out to in actuality be Yuuko using a false EDEN avatar modeled after her older brother. Rie informs Yuuko that she'd imbued the avatar with an artificial personality that she had used to manipulate Yuko's actions, and begins a process of extracting Yuuko's memories. Omnimon's restoration to his form causes him to remember that his true purpose of coming to EDEN was to save the Digital World from an infestation of Eaters, which were created from negative human emotions taking form in EDEN. The Digital World's ruler, King Drasil , had determined that humans were the cause, and its Royal Knights were split in deciding whether or not its will was to destroy humanity to eradicate the Eaters. Deducing that Rie's plan is to open a dimensional door to allow the Royal Knights in, Aiba and their friends chase after her in order to stop her and save Yuuko, but due to the interference of Suedou, who reveals that he was the one who had handed out the Digimon Capture, they fail to stop her from opening the gate and revealing herself to be the Royal Knight Crusadermon . The group then attempts to save Yuuko, who has been absorbed by Eater into an entity called Eater Eve , but even after defeating it Yuuko refuses to emerge from her despair at being manipulated. Aiba, realizing that Eater is digital and they can Connect Jump into it. With the help of Fei's TigerVespamon , they convince Yuuko that she's not alone and get her out, but Aiba is pulled into a digital void; there, they meet the real Yuugo Kamishiro , Yuuko's brother and a victim of Eater. sections.title: Development
sections.content_html:
The game features CG cutscenes made by Kamikazedouga. German subtitles were added in a free patch on September 15, 2017.

The Steam port was done by H.a.n.d..

Cyber Sleuth is considered to be a reboot of the Digimon Story (series) and was developed with player feedback in mind. Kazumasa Habu decided to stick to the base concepts of the Story series which has simple turn based battles with a levelling system, as that would allow players to be able to play without having to read instructions. As the focus of the Story series was to collect and train Digimon, it was felt that it was important to make sure Cyber Sleuth at least had the same amount of trainable Digimon as the original Digimon Story game, Digimon World DS. With Cyber Sleuth having 3D models instead of sprites this was tough, but they were able to achieve this goal thanks to the work of the developers, Media.Vision. Feedback they had received from players was that they wanted to be able to see their Digimon during battle, which the Nintendo DS games didn't do, which is why they decided to use 3D models for Cyber Sleuth. Due to the experience of creating models for Digimon Adventure (PSP), Habu was certain they would be able to take that knowledge into making them for Cyber Sleuth as well. The attack and victory animations in Cyber Sleuth were very popular and highly admired, with their quality being because one of the development staff was a big Digimon fan so put a lot of effort into studying even minor Digimon. When Cyber Sleuth was in development, overseas distributors were not open to the idea of localising Digimon games because according to them, the games were aimed at children, and the anime wasn't popular, but they were eventually to localise Cyber Sleuth because of the petitions signed by fans for Digimon games to be localised again.

The English release of Cyber Sleuth added new content, including a Hard Mode, New Game+, and two exclusive Digimon, Beelzemon BM and Kerpymon (Black). A month after the English release, seven new Digimon were added as DLC (ShineGreymon BM, MirageGaogamon BM, Rosemon BM, Ravemon BM, Valkyrimon, Chaosmon, and Darkdramon). All of these revisions other than Beelzemon and Kerpymon were later patched into the Japanese versions of the game.

sections.title: Gameplay
sections.content_html:
Digi-Lab: Allows Aiba to digivolve/degenerate their Digimon. Aiba can also store Digimon in the Digi-Bank, or send them to one of five Digi-Farms. Mirei Mikagura owns the Digi-Lab and allows Aiba to access it. The Digi-Lab also features a store, which sells Farm Goods, Mirror Dungeons - which allow access to one time only dungeons that have already been completed and counter that allows Aiba to battle Aibas from alternate universes.

Digi-Farm: A feature inside the Digi-Lab. By using Farm Expansion kits, Aiba can get up to five Digi-Farms, which can store ten Digimon each. The Digimon on the farm can be fed various foods, all of which boost stats. The food can either be bought in the Digi-Lab, is rewarded through missions or is found in chests in various dungeons. By using Farm Development kits, Aiba can add up to five Farm Goods, which when training boost stats of the Digimon in the farm. In addition to the stats provided by the farm goods, the farm leader's personality will also boost the Digimon's stats, though unlike previous Story games - these bonus stats are tied to the ABI stat. If wanting to lower any of these stats, Aiba can purchase restraint chips, which will lower bonus stats from training. Aiba can set the Digimon to train which will increase stats, based on the ABI, farm goods and leader personality. Digimon can train for either 30 minutes, 60 minutes or 120 minutes. Choosing the quicker options yields results faster but will lower the CAM stat. In addition, Digimon can also be sent to develop items, or find repeatable farm cases, with the same 30/60/120 minute options.

Digivolve: Here, Aiba can digivolve or de-digivolve their Digimon. The requirements to digivolve to a higher form are identical no matter the lower form, whilst the requirements to de-digivolve to a lower form are: "You have discovered this Digimon before". If the Digimon has not been recorded in their Field Guide, they cannot De-Digivolve into a lower form but can digivolve into higher forms they have yet to see, provided they meet all the requirements. Once a Digimon digivolves or de-digivolves, their level will reset to level 1, however their ABI and maximum level will increase. Digimon stats are fixed and will never change, so a level 50 Agumon will always have the same stats as every other level 50 Agumon, the only customisation being the use of bonus stats, tied to the ABI stat and the personality, which boosts a one stats by 5%. There are some Digimon, that even at level 99, will be unable to digivolve into some of their higher forms, meaning the Digimon must be trained to reach the required stats. A Digimon can only have a maximum of 20 moves, meaning moves will need to be delete should a Digimon learn a 21st attack.

The personalities are as follows:

  • Durable: Increases HP.
  • Lively: Increases SP.
  • Fighter: Increases ATK.
  • Defender: Increases DEF.
  • Brainy: Increases INT.
  • Nimble: Increases SPD.
  • Builder: Provides faster and better quality returns on Item Development.
  • Searcher: Provide faster and better quality returns on Investigations.

Aiba can purchase patches in EDEN to change a Digimon's personality.

The stats are as follows:

  • HP: The amount of HP the Digimon has. When a Digimon's HP reaches 0, they cannot battle any more.
  • SP: The amount of SP the Digimon has. Every attack, other than the generic attack, takes a certain amount of SP, which is taken from the overall SP. If the Digimon does not have enough SP, it cannot use the move.
  • ATK: The damage of Physical Attacks is based on how high the ATK stat if the attacking Digimon is.
  • DEF: The damage of Physical Attacks is based on how high the DEF stat of the defending Digimon is.
  • INT: The damage of Magic Attacks is based on how high the INT stat is of the attacking Digimon is and how high the INT stat is of the defending Digimon. INT also effects how much HP is healed when using healing attacks.
  • SPD: The turn order is decided in order of each Digimon's SPD stats. The higher the SPD is compared to the other Digimon, the more turns the Digimon will get. If the SPD stat is high enough, Digimon can get multiple turns in a row.
  • CAM: CAM maxes out at 100. The higher the CAM of a Digimon is, the more likely they are to do Cross Combos. Cross Combos have Digimon teaming up to do their special attack, taking only SP from the commanding Digimon. Digimon must be next to each other in the attack list to do Cross Combos. CAM increase by 1 each time a Digimon is in the active party at the end of a battle.
  • ABI: ABI maxes out at 100. The higher the ABI, the more bonus stats can be trained, with the amount being equal to 50+half the ABI stat, maxing out at 100. ABI is increased by Digivolving and De-Digivolving, though some food also increase the ABI stat.

Digimon Capture: Every time Aiba fights wild Digimon in battle (not including boss fights), the program will scan all the Digimon's data. The higher levelled the Digimon, the less data it scans. When reaching 100% scan, Aiba can create their own version of the Digimon. Unlike previous Story games, which max out at 999%, Cyber Sleuth scan data maxes out at 200%. Creating a Digimon with more than 100% scan data will cause the Digimon to start with a higher ABI, starting at 0 ABI at 100% scan, and 5 ABI at 200%. Aiba can also return Digimon to 100% scan data, as well as load Digimon into other Digimon, permanently deleting them, turning them into experience points for the Digimon absorbing the Deleted Digimon.

Memory: Aiba is allowed to store up to 11 Digimon in their Digi-vice at once, with three acting in the battle slots. Memory acts as a capacity limitation, with more powerful Digimon taking up more memory. As an example, should Aiba have 20 memory, they could store 10 Training I Digimon in their digivice, who all take 2 memory or take a lower amount of Digimon of higher levels, such as four 5 memory Rookie level Digimon. Memory can increased by using Memory Ups and Memory UP DX, which add 5 and 10 memory respectively, which can be found in chests, drop from boss fights or are rewards from completing missions.

Battle System:. Like previous Story games, battles are random encounters and allow fights against up to 3 Digimon. The 3 Digimon n the active party slots will be used in battle, though should Aiba have less than three Digimon, one/two will be used. Aiba can also willingly used less than three Digimon by only assigning one or two Digimon to the active party slots. Battles are turn based, with the attack order being based on the SPD of the Digimon in battle. Aiba can do the following commands:

  • Attack: The chosen Digimon will do a generic attack, that takes no SP.
  • Skill: The chosen Digimon will do the chosen attack, provided the Digimon has enough SP.
  • Guard: The chosen Digimon will take no action and will instead guard, which will half the damage of any attacks that hit them until their next turn.
  • Item: Aiba can use an item.
  • Escape: Aiba and their Digimon will escape the battle. Some battles cannot be escaped from.
  • Change: Aiba can switch out any of the active battle Digimon, with any of the reserve Digimon, including Digimon with no HP, the switch taking the turn of the Digimon who's turn was used to do the switch. The turn order will change based on the SPD stats of the new Digimon and continue as normal.
  • Auto: The battle speeds up and the Digimon choose their attacks on their own. Commands cannot be used during Auto mode.

Attributes:

  • Fire: Strong against Plant, weak against Water.
  • Plant: Strong against Water, weak against Fire.
  • Water: Strong against Fire, weak against Plant.
  • Electric: Strong against Wind, weak against Earth.
  • Wind: Strong against Earth, weak against Electric.
  • Earth: Strong against Electric, weak against Wind.
  • Light: Strong against Dark, weak against Dark.
  • Dark: Strong against Light, weak against Light.
  • Neutral: Strong against and weak against nothing.

Types

  • Vaccine: Strong against Virus, weak against and does half damage to Data
  • Data: Strong against Vaccine and weak against and does half damage to Virus.
  • Virus: Strong against Data and weak against and does half damage to Vaccine.
  • Free: Strong against and weak against nothing.

A double advantage can be reached if a Digimon with a Type advantage uses a move with a Attribute advantage over another Digimon. The opposite happens if a Digimon with a Type disadvantage uses a move with an attribute disadvantage. For example, A Vaccine Digimon using a Fire Attribute attack will do x3 damage against a Digimon that is Virus/Plant, whilst using the same move against a Data type will do x0.5 damage. A Vaccine Digimon can boost their damage to 0.75% if they attack a Data Digimon with a move that is strong against the Data Digimon's Attribute, such as using a Fire Attribute attack against a Data/Plant Digimon. A Digimon attacking another Digimon with a Attribute Advantage will do x2 damage, or x1.25 if both Digimon are the same type, or if the Digimon is Free type.

The Complete Edition includes the Gameplay changes from Hacker's Memory, with the exception of Domination Battles. This version originally released in Japan on PS4/Vita in 2017, and was not released in English until 2019 on Switch/PC (with the name Complete Edition being exclusive to the English release).

When reaching 100% scan, Aiba can create their own version of the Digimon. Unlike previous Story games, which max out at 999%, Cyber Sleuth scan data maxes out at 200%. Creating a Digimon with more than 100% scan data will cause the Digimon to start with a higher ABI, starting at 0 ABI at 100% scan, and 5 ABI at 200%. Aiba can also return Digimon to 100% scan data, as well as load Digimon into other Digimon, permanently deleting them, turning them into experience points for the Digimon absorbing the Deleted Digimon. Memory: Aiba is allowed to store up to 11 Digimon in their Digi-vice at once, with three acting in the battle slots. Memory acts as a capacity limitation, with more powerful Digimon taking up more memory. As an example, should Aiba have 20 memory, they could store 10 Training I Digimon in their digivice, who all take 2 memory or take a lower amount of Digimon of higher levels, such as four 5 memory Rookie level Digimon. Memory can increased by using Memory Ups and Memory UP DX, which add 5 and 10 memory respectively, which can be found in chests, drop from boss fights or are rewards from completing missions. Battle System: . Like previous Story games, battles are random encounters and allow fights against up to 3 Digimon. The 3 Digimon n the active party slots will be used in battle, though should Aiba have less than three Digimon, one/two will be used. Aiba can also willingly used less than three Digimon by only assigning one or two Digimon to the active party slots. Battles are turn based, with the attack order being based on the SPD of the Digimon in battle. Aiba can do the following commands: Attack: The chosen Digimon will do a generic attack, that takes no SP. Skill: The chosen Digimon will do the chosen attack, provided the Digimon has enough SP. Guard: The chosen Digimon will take no action and will instead guard, which will half the damage of any attacks that hit them until their next turn. Item: Aiba can use an item. Escape: Aiba and their Digimon will escape the battle. Some battles cannot be escaped from. Change: Aiba can switch out any of the active battle Digimon, with any of the reserve Digimon, including Digimon with no HP, the switch taking the turn of the Digimon who's turn was used to do the switch. The turn order will change based on the SPD stats of the new Digimon and continue as normal. Auto: The battle speeds up and the Digimon choose their attacks on their own. Commands cannot be used during Auto mode. Attributes: Fire: Strong against Plant, weak against Water. Plant: Strong against Water, weak against Fire. Water: Strong against Fire, weak against Plant. Electric: Strong against Wind, weak against Earth. Wind: Strong against Earth, weak against Electric. Earth: Strong against Electric, weak against Wind. Light: Strong against Dark, weak against Dark. Dark: Strong against Light, weak against Light. Neutral: Strong against and weak against nothing. Types Vaccine: Strong against Virus, weak against and does half damage to Data Data: Strong against Vaccine and weak against and does half damage to Virus. Virus: Strong against Data and weak against and does half damage to Vaccine. Free: Strong against and weak against nothing. A double advantage can be reached if a Digimon with a Type advantage uses a move with a Attribute advantage over another Digimon. The opposite happens if a Digimon with a Type disadvantage uses a move with an attribute disadvantage. For example, A Vaccine Digimon using a Fire Attribute attack will do x3 damage against a Digimon that is Virus/Plant, whilst using the same move against a Data type will do x0.5 damage. A Vaccine Digimon can boost their damage to 0.75% if they attack a Data Digimon with a move that is strong against the Data Digimon's Attribute, such as using a Fire Attribute attack against a Data/Plant Digimon. A Digimon attacking another Digimon with a Attribute Advantage will do x2 damage, or x1.25 if both Digimon are the same type, or if the Digimon is Free type. The Complete Edition includes the Gameplay changes from Hacker's Memory , with the exception of Domination Battles . This version originally released in Japan on PS4/Vita in 2017, and was not released in English until 2019 on Switch/PC (with the name Complete Edition being exclusive to the English release).

sections.title: Obtainable Digimon
sections.content_html:
The original version of Cyber Sleuth includes 249 Digimon, including Digimon which, outside of Europe, were exclusive to pre-orders. Like previous Story games, the player can access a Field Guide which depicts the Digimon's model, attack, and walking animations, their base stats, the attacks they can learn, and their background profile. Cyber Sleuth adds the ability to show the stat growth from level 1 thru 99, as well as their Digivolution paths.

The Complete Edition adds the 92 Digimon introduced in Hacker's Memory.

sections.title: Reception
sections.content_html: The Entermix magazine named Cyber Sleuth the best game of 2015. By May 2019, Cyber Sleuth had sold over 800,000 copies worldwide. By October 2020, Hacker's Memory and Cyber Sleuth had shipped more than 1.5 million units worldwide combined. By March 2025, they had sold a combined 2.5 million, and by May 2026, 3 million.

sections.title: Other Notes
sections.content_html:
Continuity errors

  • In the English version, the subtitles have Nokia incorrectly say "DigiFuse" instead of "DNA Digivolve" when Omnimon is formed for the first time.

Animation errors

  • In all languages, MirageGaogamon BM's Special Skill Mirage Burst states it increases INT by 13%, however it actually increases EVA not INT.

Dubbing changes

  • Due to a translation error, multiple characters refer to Eaters as "Bakemon", as "Bakemono" (monster) is similar to "Bakemon" and occasionally actually spoken as "Bakemon".
  • At one point in the English version, Matayoshi refers to Crusadermon as its Japanese name "LordKnightmon", rather than the name used in the game, "Crusadermon".

Digimon references

  • The cover art depicts Agumon resting on Nokia's head, similarly to the covers of Digimon World Re:Digitize and Digimon World Re:Digitize: Decode, which depict Agumon resting on Taiga's head. All three games had Suzuhito Yasuda as the character designer.

Real-world references

  • At some point, a Digimon in the Digi-Farm will send a DigiLine message stating they have read The Vamdemon of the Opera (オペラ座のヴァンデモン, Opera-za no Vandemon?), a reference to The Phantom of the Opera.

Miscellaneous trivia

  • Cyber Sleuth and Digimon World: Next Order are shown in a game store in Sword Art Online Alternative Gun Gale Online episode 2.
  • In Japan, four PSN themes were released to promote both Cyber Sleuth and the video game Sword Art Online: Lost Song. They feature Agumon and Kirito.
  • The arcade has Tekken posters.

sections.title: Side Missions
sections.content_html:
Mystery of the Missing T-Shirt

Hiroko Sagisaka texts Yuki, saying that T-Shirts are going missing and to come to Kosuke Misono's office as it may be an anomaly. She says it may be a ghost stealing them, since a human would've been caught by now, and so they should look into it. The owner of the shop says the shirts fly away on their own, and that it had actually happened just before they arrived. They follow a customer into an alley, who says he saw a monster go into the sewers with the T-Shirt. Inside, they find a ZubaEagermon wondering how it can make the stolen T-Shirts "scream Twentiest". Hiroko and Yuki confront him, and he asks them if they're Twentiest. They have no idea what tha means, and their answer on how to make the shirt Twentiest angers him. As such, Yuki and Aegiomon fight him. They defeat him and take all the stolen T-Shirts back, though Hiroko says they now have to figure out what Twentiest is. The shopkeeper thanks them for solving it, and says he'll give them discounts if they ever buy from him.

The Targeted Cosplayer

Hiroko Sagisaka texts Yuki, saying a cosplayer had gone missing in Shinjuku Park. Yuki, Hiroko, Aegiomon, and Minervamon go to the park, where Hiroko had agreed to meet with the cosplayer's friend. She explains how the friend had gone missing whilst cosplaying in the park, and Hiroko decides to recreate the moment by forcing Yuki to cosplay as one of the Chosen Children from Digimon Adventure (Kanan as Kari Kamiya, Dan as Taichi "Tai" Kamiya). When Yuki starts walking around in the outfit, a portal opens and sucks them both in. They end up in the same place as the cosplayer, who tells them to get away before the monster returns. Tuskmon shows up and is happy at having finally caught a Tamer, and attacks them so they can't run away — saying their master would be mad if it lost the Tamer. After they kill Tuskmon, Hiroko asks if the cosplayer knows the master, though she says no as she only saw Tuskmon. As they wonder how they can return, they're sucked into another portal that takes them back. The cosplayer's friend thanks them for saving her, whilst Hiroko continues to wonder who Tuskmon's master was.

Infinite Imagination

Hiroko Sagisaka says she got a tip from a social media fan about an anomaly. The fan had created their own character, and that their character's data had disappeared one day. Shortly afterwards, they got messages telling them to go to a back alley in Akihabara. This scared them, hence Hiroko. They, Aegiomon, and Minervamon search around Akihabara, and eventually find a bunch of giant plastic blocks. When they try to investigate it, Shota Kuroi tells them to stay away as Public Security was already investigating it. He says they're not regular blocks, and that Monica Simmons' device had gotten readings from it — as well as similar readings nearby. Unable to leave his post, he winds up agreeing to let them look around. They find two more blocks around Akihabara and return, which causes the bricks to combine and come to life as a giant ToyAgumon. ToyAgumon says it's lonely and wants to play — then attacks them. After they defeat it, it disappears. Shota says it's a strange dangerous creature that can't be allowed to roam free, which offends Hiroko since a kid made it. After Shota leaves to report what happened, Hiroko says the kid is lonely as has no friends and his parents are never around — hence why he made ToyAgumon. She then figured the kid's feelings effected ToyAgumon and that it didn't mean to rampage.

To Do the Job, You Need to Dress the Part

Asuna Shiroki puts out a message saying how many Public Safety staff had gone on leave, causing a staff shortage — and that she needed an energy drink. Yuki takes on the mission, and goes to Akihabara to find her — where Asuna complains about being overworked. Asuna is surprised someone took the request, and assumes she's hallucinating from too many energy drinks. Feeling it's fine to accept help sometimes, she has Yuki go with her to the underground. She has Yuki wear a Public Safety outfit so they can pass as actual staff, with Shota Kuroi annoyed she'd dragged a civilian in to help. An Outer Dungeon suddenly shows up in the middle of his complaining, and so the three of them go into it. They find two Bakemon inside, and defeat them. After the battle, Shota says if Yuki ever impersonates Public Safety again — he'll arrest them. He says he heard the government had sent agents to dig up info on Digimon, assumes Yuki is one of them — tells them to stay out of their business and says they will not be allies the next time they meet.

The Secret Getaway

Hiroko Sagisaka tells Yuki she got more information from social media, with people saying ghosts had been seen in Shinjuku Park. Asuna Shiroki approaches them whilst they're looking around the park and says they should stay away from the forest as she had heard an odd cry there the other day. Instead of heading the warning, Hiroko says she'll help out by using her camera — which Asuna agrees to since video footage may come in handy. Once there, they hear the cries — and quickly find they belong to a Guilmon. It's only able to say its own name, and despite that, Yuki is seemingly able to have a conversation with it by saying "Guil" a bunch of times. It runs into the sewers, with the others following it. When they find it, it attacks them. After defeating it, they note it seemed to just be playing with them and decide not to follow it further into the sewers since it didn't seem to be a threat.

The Father of Shinjuku

Hiroko Sagisaka tells Yuki she had managed to get a reservation with the famous fortune teller in Koshu-Kaido, and asks them to come with her. The fortune teller, known as "The Father of Shinjuku", does Hiroko's reading, and, aware she's a streamer, tells her she can achieve her dream and to be kind to everyone she meets...not just humans. After Hiroko leaves, he motions to do Yuki's fortune — only for Yuki to say they know he's not a human. He says his species isn't important, and that he knew Yuki would arrive today. He asks them to find four Digimon in the real world, as they had gotten lost and were unable to find their way home. He sends them them out to find them one by one, with Yuki's job made harder by the fact the four of them were disguised as humans. Yuki eventually tracks Gaomon, Lalamon, Bukamon, and Datamon down and takes them to fortune teller so he can send them back to Digital World: Iliad. As thanks for helping him, he reveals he's actually AncientWisemon in disguise — though Yuki isn't surprised. This annoys AncientWisemon, as he thought he'd done a good job pretending to be a human.

Between the Worlds

Hiroko Sagisaka texts Yuki saying she's located an anomaly in Akihabara and to meet there. Once there, Yuki finds not Hiroko, but Agumon, who was in front of an Outer Dungeon. He says he has lost Gabumon and was warned to prevent that from happening. He's surprised to see Yuki, but figures it's fine since they have their own Digimon. They go inside, and find Gabumon fighting an Orochimon. Now re-united, they Warp DNA Digivolve together into Omnimon then defeat it with Yuki's help. Once they come out of the Dungeon, they land right in front of Hiroko and Public Safety. Hiroko is annoyed Yuki went without them, and says she hadn't shown up because she had been caught by Public Safety. Yuki lies and says Agumon and Gabumon are their partners to try and keep them safe, but Agumon corrects them and says they already have a partner. He says they need to leave before they get in trouble with their boss, and the duo escape before they can be captured. Public Safety say trouble always happens around Yuki and Hiroko, and as such — they're going to keep a closer eye on the two of them. Hiroko and Asuna Shiroki bond over liking Agumon and Gabumon, leading an annoyed Shota Kuroi to remind her she's at work. Public Safety decide to look around for anything left behind — whilst Yuki and Hiroko leave.

A Delayed Return

A Hagurumon in Central Town says its colleague should be back by now, since the next shift should've started. Yuki overhears and asks what's wrong, with it saying that its friend may be in trouble...though it may also just be asleep since it's lazy. Since it's off duty and isn't allowed to do overtime, it asks Yuki to go check on it in its place. Yuki travels over to Central Tower, and finds the Hagurumon really was asleep. They wake it up, and it panics and leaves since it's not meant to be doing overtime. When Yuki returns, original Hagurumon thanks them for helping out.

The Blacksmith's Request

Zudomon asks Yuki to get him some materials from Central Tower. After Yuki gets them, he thanks them by allowing them to use his store.

Knowledge Is the Death of Fear

An Agumon texts Yuki, saying that some Digimon are scared of humans and that it will visit their house to talk about it. It shows up with Gatomon, who suggests the humans dress up as Digimon to try and make it easier for the scared Digimon to talk to them. Even Aegiomon has to, since they consider him a human due to how much time he spends with them. They go to Patamon and Palmon, who were scared of humans, and are able to befriend them — their Digimon costumes helping. Agumon and Gatomon then thank them for helping their friends get over their phobias.

From Pegasusmon to the World

Pegasusmon texts Yuki saying there's something it wants to do and that it needs their help. It says its there to encourage everyone, and that it needs to keep it up. Yuki notices Pegasusmon's worry, with Pegasusmon saying it can't be helped. Struggling to put its thoughts into words, it wonders if it can use its actions and asks Yuki for Digi-Eggs so its friends can digivolve and get stronger. Yuki has none, leading Pegasusmon to suggest asking Vulcanusmon to make them. He makes them for Yuki, and Yuki returns to Pegasusmon. Pegasusmon uses them on his friends, who Armor Digivolve. The four newly digivolved Armor Digimon join Yuki's party, with Yuki either leaving them in Central Town to protect it or taking them on their journey to fight the Titans.

Back to the Skies

Andromon talks to Yuki about how badly damaged Blimpmon is, and says it'll need a large amount of metal to fix him. Yuki asks the nearby Guardromon for metal, which it happily gives since it was thanks to them production was going smoothly again. Yuki gives it to Andromon, who then repairs Blimpmon.

Quick to Fight, Quick on the Job

Guardromon says to Yuki that the production lines are inoperative, and that the cause is insufficient material. It says LoaderLeomon is the one who moves production material from the mines, and that they've lost contact with it. It asks them to go and find LoaderLeomon and tell it the Titan issue is over and that it needs to deliver the Chrondigizoit Ore. Yuki goes into the mine and finds LoaderLeomon on a drilling rampage, and it attacks them thinking they're a Titan looking to stop its fun. Yuki tells it to contact Guadromon, and it does so saying Titans had shown up in the mine. Guadromon tells it about how the Titans were gone thanks to Yuki, and LoaderLeomon apologizes. They go to Guardromon with its drilled up metals, and says it's realized it's supposed to take the metal to the residents — not just spend all day having fun drilling.

The Trial

Solarmon talks to Yuki about how it can't get a Parrotmon plume for Bearmon from Central Tower because the Titans are in the way. It leaves for the tower, with Yuki following it. Yuki agrees to help, and finds one after defeating the Titans there. Solarmon thanks them, and gives them some items as a reward.

The Craftsman's Partner

Zudomon tells Yuki its hammer is broken, and asks them to get it some Chrondigizoit Metal so it can fix it. Yuki gets some from Guadromon, and gives it Zudomon. Zudomon uses it to fix its hammer.

I Want to Go Someplace Legendary!

With Blimpmon fixed, Coronamon says he wants to go on a trip to the Cosmic Area so he can train there and become strong. Blimpmon tells him he can't take him, as the area is the weather there is both too hot and cold. This relieves Lunamon and disappoints Coronamon. Yuki asks if there was any way he could go, with Blimpmon saying he'd be able to he it had a heater and a cooler. Yuki says they'll get them, with Blimpmon surprised at just how much they wanted to help Coronamon and Lunamon. He says there might be a cooler in the Factorial Area, with Yuki leaving to go find one. Yuki asks Vademon if he has any, and he offers to sell one for 10 million yen. Yuki is able to haggle the price down to 1000 yen, and buys it. They take it Blimpmon, who gets Datamon to install it. He says to tell Coronamon the good news, with a disappointed Lunamon saying guess we're going to Heat Cosmic. Coronamon surprises Lunamon and says he's going alone as only one Digimon can be the strongest. Lunamon protests, but Coronamon gets on Blimpmon before she can finish talking. Blimpmon then flies away. Lunamon worries about him, though quickly changes to anger and says she'll get Minervamon to beat him up when he gets back.

Platinum Numemon's Jewelry

Yuki comes across the Bearmon Brothers and Solarmon whilst in Central Town. Big Bearmon praises Solarmon, saying it brought him a plume, and that it's way cooler than Yuki — unaware it was actually Yuki who got the plume. He offers Yuki a chance to "redeem themselves", and that they're going to the underground to steal PlatinumNumemon's jewelry. Once inside, the group beat up a group of Geremon under the mistaken assumption they were PlatinumNumemon. The actual PlatinumNumemon was watching the battle, with the group unaware. They look around for the jewelry, and find some cut glass. Solarmon and Little Bearmon think its treasure, though Big Bearmon is fully aware it's worthless and says they need the find the real jewelry. They say they're tired, and will just have to try again another day. They say they should ask at the tavern about the jewelry, and leave. Having heard this tip, Yuki goes there before them and talks to Deputymon about what happened. He tells them the Digimon they fought weren't PlatinumNumemon, and that the real one is Platinum and hangs out deep in the sewers. Yuki travels through the entire sewer, but is unable to find it...unaware it was following them the entire time. Yuki returns to the entrance, and just before leaving — turns around. They finally see PlatinumNumemon, and have their Digimon defeat it — acquiring the jewelry. Yuki shows off it off the trio, and Big Bearmon asks if he can have it. Yuki says they'll trade for it, and Big Bearmon offer to give them their special item for it — despite Little Bearmon's protests. Yuki then either does the trade, or gives it them for free.

A Missing Friend

Whilst in Central Town, Yuki sees a Motimon telling Agumon and Gabumon that its and its friends had been attacked whilst they were playing in the the Abyss Area. This caused them to get split up. Unfamiliar with Digital World: Iliad, they say have no clue what could've attacked them. Yuki asks if they can help, and they happily allow them to join the search. They go to to the Abyss Area, and find a Punimon being attacked by one of the remaining Titan — Scorpiomon. Agumon and Gabumon become Omnimon and defeat it with Yuki's help. Punimon thanks them for saving it, though quickly realises Motimon wasn't around. The group calm it down and take it to Central Town, reuniting the two baby Digimon. They offer them a reward, with the Yuki taking it since Agumon and Gabumon had no use for it. Agumon wonders what the Titans were up to, and he and Gabumon leave to look into it.

Impatience and Determination

Lunamon texts Yuki, saying she can't go on like this and to come talk to her. Blimpmon had returned from the Cosmic Area, but Coronamon hadn't — and Lunamon felt like she needed to take action. She says she needs to go to the Cosmic Area too, though decides she'd rather not go to the same place Coronamon went to — so decides to go to Chill Cosmic instead of Heat Cosmic. Blimpmon says he can't go as he doesn't have a heater, and has no idea where to get one. Yuki says they'll find one, and Blimpmon excitedly says he knows they'll be able to find one. Lunamon says she'll help look, and remembers seeing one inside one of of the houses in Central Town. Whilst checking houses, Yuki come across a Betamon who says its heater had been stolen by a Goblimon. Yuki says they'll track it down, though Betamon says it doesn't matter as it was faulty so it was just gong to buy a new one. Yuki finds a group of Goblimon in town and asks if one of them stole a heater, with the thief surprised Yuki knew. Yuki retries the heater and takes it to Blimpmon. Lunamo arrives and says she couldn't find one, though Blimpmon says it doesn't matter as it has one now. Blimpmon has Datamon fix it and install it, then takes Lunamon to Chill Cosmic.

The Color the Water Speaks Of

A Kamemon texts Yuki, saying they're all alone and is having trouble with something. It says it thinks the the Titans didn't leave because of Yuki, they probably left because they'd already achieved everything they wanted to. It notes the sea breeze smells different, and that Shellmon would know if something was up if she was here. They go to Shellmon's house in the hopes they could find a device to measure water quality. They find Shellmon's diary and end up reading it, with Kamemon finding an entry about water quality. If the plants are blue, it's fine — if they're purple, they're hurtful. It even says where the exact plants to check are. They go there, though Kamemon says it can't swim — meaning Yuki has to. Yuki swims through a group of Syakomon, and eventually finds the specific plant. It's purple, meaning the water is contaminated. This has it realize why the breeze smelled off, and it gives them items as thanks. It says it'll stay in the area and keep an eye on things.

Divermon's Woes

Divermon texts Yuki, saying how it was weird that Sharkmon backed down and that they should investigate the ocean floor. They travel around with the help of Submarimon, and find a spot where it's hard to breathe. They hear a voice saying to "give it back", and get attacked by a Crabmon who demands they return the current. Crabmon doesn't remember anything after the battle, and last remembered struggling to breathe. Divermon says he was right, and that he knew Sharkmon wouldn't have gone down quietly. He had clearly done something to the current. Divermon says his new plan was to become leader of the ocean Titans in Sharkmon's place, and that when becomes leader he'll order them to not cause any trouble. They then leave the area to avoid losing their minds like Crabmon had.

Proper Beach Attire

A Wanyamon from Central Town messages Yuki, saying they'd gone to the Abyss Area but that no one was there. When Yuki, Inori Misono, and Aegiomon arrive, it asks them to put on swimsuits and then swim in the ocean with it. They get changed and go there, but get attacked by a territorial Seadramon. After they win, it flees and says it's telling its boss. MegaSeadramon and WaruSeadramon show up, upset they had beat up Seadramon — and attack them assuming they're Titans. After losing, they also say they're going to tell their boss — though MetalSeadramon shows up and says they don't need to as Seadramon had already told it about the Titan invasion. It misunderstandings them wanting to have fun in the ocean as invading, and attacks them as well. Once defeated, MetalSeadramon surrenders and says the ocean is theirs. They turn it down and say they're not Titans, and tell them they're the ones who defeated the Titans in the first place. MetalSeadramon apologizes, and lets them play. They play together in the the water for a while, with Wanyamon rewarding them as thanks once they're done.

Secret of the Hidden Honey Base

A Muchomon texts Yuki, saying it had been attacked by bees. When Yuki goes to it, it says there's a hidden honey base belonging to the FunBeemon nearby, and that they had attacked it when it tried to steal some of the honey. It says there are probably Digimon scared of them, and then says the Titans were probably behind it and plan to immobilize everyone with FunBeemon. Yuki believes this, and Muchomon sends them to destroy the honey base. They destroy it, beat up all the FunBeemon, and return to Muchomon — who thanks them for doing so.

The Mighty Bearmon Brothers

The Bearmon Brothers message Yuki, saying they're going to patrol Gear Forest to keep it safe. Yuki travels there and finds them searching for Titans. Yuki tells them they had already defeated the Titans, which upsets the Bearmon Brothers. They decide the ones Yuki defeated were just small fry, and figure the real ones must be hiding somewhere. Big Bearmon runs off to go find the supposed bosses, leaving Little Bearmon behind since he was worried about them fighting the bosses. Little Bearmon asks for Yuki's help, and Yuki agrees. They search around and are actually able to find a member of the Titans, Minotarumon. After defeating it, Little Bearmon worries his brother was fighting one too — and so they look around for him. They find him fighting Greymon, another Titan, and help him defeat it. Big Bearmon says they aren't strong enough as they are right now, and Little Bearmon becomes upset realizing his brother doesn't want to be with him any more. Big Bearmon says there may be times they're not together, and so they need to be strong enough to fight by themselves. He has them promise that no matter what happens between them, they would meet again at the nearby tree. They thank Yuki for their help, and give them a reward. Yuki checks out the tree, and sees they had buried a note in a box saying the two brothers would bring peace to Digital World: Iliad together.

Listen to the Voice

JumboGamemon texts Yuki, saying its stuck in stuck in jail in the Abyss Sanctuary. When Yuki arrives, it says it was the Kamemon they knew eight years ago and had found a vein of Chrondigizoit Ore there but had also managed to get stuck in a Titan trap. It says it had tried to break out, but that the cell was too strong. Yuki realizes only Neptunemon could help, and says they'll go talk to him. JumboGamemon is happy to hear this, saying the other Digimon hadn't listened to him and had refused to help. Yuki explains this to Neptunemon, who is shocked to hear about such cells. He agrees to free it, and JumboGamemon is shocked they were able to get Neptunemon to come. He apologizes for not coming sooner, and frees it — also saying he was impressed it had found the ore. Neptunemon asks it to come with him, but it refuses as it doesn't trust him. Neptuemon promises to never have him go through something so bad again, and it decides to trust him. Neptunemon thanks Yuki, and rewards them.

Message from Beyond Time

Big Drimogemon and Little Drimogemon message Yuuki, saying they will defeat the Titans and make Gear Forest peaceful again. When Yuki goes to them, they talk about how they were inspired by the legendary Bearmon Brothers. They argue about if they should go left or right, and end the argument ends up so bad that they end their brothership. Yuki finds Little Drimogemon fighting a Groundramon and helps him defeat it. After the battle, Little Drimogemon says he's sad about the break up and leaves to go visit the Bearmon Brother's sanctuary to think. Yuki later finds Big Drimogemon fighting a WarGrowlmon, and helps him as well. He tries to celebrate the win with his brother, though ends up remembering he's not there. Sad, he too goes to the sanctuary. Yuki finds an ashamed Little at the shrine, with him saying the legendary brothers wouldn't want him there since he argued with his own brother. Big shows up, and Little tries to apologize. Big notices something buried in the ground before he can though, and the two brothers dig it up. They uncover the note the Bearmon Brothers had written eight years in the past, and figure it must've come to them as the the legendary brothers were telling them to always stick together. They make up and keep the note as a symbol of the lesson they learned from the legendary brothers. They then reward Yuki as thanks for helping them beat up some Titans.

Hidden Honey Base Strikes Back

Peckmon messages Yuki, saying the Gear Forest is in trouble because of the bees. When Yuki goes to Peckmon, it says it was the Muchomon who had asked them to deal with the FunBeemon eight years earlier. It shows Yuki a letter it got, which demands the one who destroyed their bases goes to the Shade Tree Pier so that they can get their revenge — and if they don't, the bees would attack the village. Peckmon had realized the bees weren't Titans, and says to try and sort things out with them. Yuki finds a TigerVespamon at the base, who was a digivolved FunBeemon that had been waiting to years get revenge. Yuki defeats it, and it submits itself to Yuki saying the strong controls the weak. Yuki tries to befriend it, though it refuses and instead decides to retire and move into the village. When they return to Peckmon, it says TigeVespamon showed up and asked to help rebuild the town and — and that Peckmon itself had apologised for assuming they were Titans and causing the entire issue.

The Greatest OMNI Carnival

Volcanomon invites Yuki and the others to the The Greatest OMNI Carnival tournament as it was impressed they were a double Champion. Yuki fights their way to the final, and eventually defeats Marsmon to become a triple champion.

How to Cheer Up a Warrior

Marsmon messages Yuki, asking what they should do with the Paradise Colosseum now Callismon was gone. When Yuki visits him, he says how sad he was about having to defeat his brother and asks what humans do to help them feel better. Yuki suggests watching a movie, and takes Marsmon to Hiroko Sagisaka. She suggests the movie "Yesterday's George", which is a boxing movie where the boxer nearly kills his opponent. Marsmon relates to this, and says he can bounce back like the boxer had. He decides to go back to the underground Colosseum, and challenges Yuki to a fight when they arrive. Yuki wins, and Marsmon realizes he's too scared to use his full strength after using it to defeat his brother. Worrying about it makes him hungry, and they agree to eat together. They eat lots of food together, which makes him feel better. He remembers his brother once saying you can't protect Digital World: Iliad on an empty stomach, and feels like he can fight again. He challenges Yuki again, and says to go to the Paradise Colosseum when they're ready for a proper rematch.

Stuck in the Restroom

A clerk at the coffee shop messages Yuki, saying someone had locked themselves in the toilet and was muttering about their captain and a weapon. Yuki says they're certain they know who it is, and is proven right when it's Shota Kuroi. They hear his complaints and knock on the door, and he recognizes Yuki's voice. Despite telling Yuki to go away, he opens up to them and talks about how much hates Digimon due to what happened to Kodai Kuremi. Yuki tries to calm him down, but he says how nothing will change his mind and that he had agreed to pilot a weapon that will let him get revenge against Digimon. He's surprised when Yuki show concern for him, and says he'll take their words into consideration. Talking about it helped him feel better, though he says it changes nothing and they're still enemies. He refuses to leave still, and Yuki leaves the shop. Seconds later, the clerk stops them says the guy came out and had asked him to give Yuki a reward as thanks.

In the Palm of an Unknown Hand

Hiroko Sagisaka messages Yuki, saying she got a creepy messages and to meet her in Higashi-Shinjuku. When they get there, she says the messages asked her to to sneak into a D-SAT vehicle and that she felt like the person had been watching her the entire time. This is proven true when she receives a new message saying to tell Yuki to dress in something cyber. Yuki puts on the same outfit Aiba wears, and they get a new message telling them to pick up an ID card and a USB drive from nearby. After they get them, they get a message telling them to get into the D-SAT vehicle in Shinjuku Park. Once they arrive, they see D-SAT staff and assume they have no chance of getting in — only to see the staff leave after getting reports that Digimon had escaped from the Digimon District. They use Kodai Kuremi's ID to get into the vehicle, then insert the USB into the computer inside after being told to do so in another message. The computer loads data about an upcoming project created by Jindai Technology, Project EDEN — as well as diary entries from a scientist who hates Yuya and Monica Simmons. Once done, they're told to leave the ID and USB on the bench nearby and that their reward is also there. Once they leave, a pleased Kyoko Kuremi says how that'll clear things up and will help her learn what "you know who" had been up to. She then leaves as well.

The Easy Road Is Best

ZubaEagermon messages Yuki, saying it was confused as it still doesn't know what "Twentiest" means and asks them to visit them in a back alley in Shinjuku. Yuki says they don't know the answer either, and it says it feels like its road to the Twentiest is gone as it doesn't know what's "in" any more. It says it's annoyed at being normal, and that the Twentiest is supposed to stand out. They mention how Yuki stands out due to their silly outfit, then realizes that helped them get closer to being the Twentiest. They ask to see more of Yuki's clothes, and specifically request clothes with Digimon on them. Yuki puts some on, and ZubeEagermon loves them so much it declares their outfit is Twentiest. It realizes being Twentiest is having extra flair that goes beyond normal fashion, and says it had been trying too hard — the more you try to be Twentiest, the further away from it you get. Having finally realized what the Twentiest is, it digivolves to Duramon. It says being normal is fine, and then says it's to going to the arena in the Factorial Area. When Yuki visits, it says it had put in "normal" effort for "normal" wins, but found it boring. It de-digivolves back to ZubaEagermon, and says it will step away from the path of the normal and will try to stand out again. It digivolves again, this time to Grademon — and says it has rediscovered the path of the Twentiest. It challenges Yuki to battle, and asks them to fight it in the Paradise Colosseum when they're ready.

I Don't Belong Anywhere Yet

MarineAngemon messages Yuki, saying that no one in the Warrior's Watering Hole respects their cuteness and that someone needs to heal their weary spirit. When Yuki visits, it says that it had wanted to be a star across the entirety of Digital World: Iliad, but that no one cared and it missed the ocean. It asks Yuki to bring it a bottle of ocean water, and so Yuki goes to the Abyss Area and gets some. Regardless of the water Yuki gets, MarineAngemon hates it as it's not from the depths. MarineAngemon runs away, and when Yuki finds it it says it'll return to the sea as that's where its fans are. When Yuki returns to the Abyss Area, they see the residents fawning over delighted MarineAngemon. It thanks Yuki and rewards them, as they were the one who got convinced it to return.

A Gift from the Hosts
