sections.title: Mistakes to avoid
sections.content_html:
There are ways to screw up in Stardew Valley. Most of them are fairly easy to avoid, but some are less obvious than others.

Don’t plant seeds that don’t have time to grow.
Plants die at the end of each season. Not all of them - Coffee is a spring-and-summer plant; Corn and Wheat are summer-and-fall plants. But most of them. So plant your recurring harvest seeds (e.g. blueberries and cranberries as early in the season as you can, and keep an eye on the date once you’ve passed the middle of the season. If your packet says 13 days - that really means 13 nights; you can plant Melons on the 15th of Summer but not the 16th. If you’ve invested in seeds when it’s just slightly too late, you may be able to save the situation with some Speed-Gro fertilizer (must be added before planting). Or you might have to stow the seeds in a chest until next year. But if you put them in the ground when they’re out of time to grow - that’s money wasted.
Don’t plant seeds you don't have energy to water.
Especially in the beginning, you will regret overplanting since there are other fun things to do. The recommended first day field size is 15 crops (Crow risk starts at 16).
Don’t forget to water your plants.
They won't die. But they won't grow either.
Don’t stay out too late.
In your first visits to the mines you’ll want to be leaving around 10 or 11pm. Staying out of bed past midnight will mean you have less energy the next day; staying up until 2am will mean you collapse, and if you’re not in your own farmhouse at that point, it’ll cost you 10% of your gold up to a maximum charge of 1000gp. Not all routes home take the same amount of time, but 2 hours will get you home from pretty much anywhere.
Don’t work until you collapse from exhaustion.
It’ll cost you, same as staying up until 2am. If you get the exhaustion warning, see if you’ve got some food you can eat - in your first spring, salmonberries and spring onions will rebuild your energy, and they sell for so little you’re better off keeping them for energy. If you don’t have food, leave the task - whatever it is, it won’t help you to collapse without finishing it - and perhaps you can go foraging instead. Or just go to bed. After 3 Summer Year 1 you can go soak in the spa to rebuild energy.
Don’t let the mine monsters kill you.
Well, it’s not really death, you lose items, money, access to levels in the mines, and you wake up with little health. It’s still a quite palpable setback. Although the game features a Potion of Life for rebuilding your health bar, you don’t need it - any old food will refill both your health and your energy bar. So take a stack of something cheap and plentiful, and eat it. In the shallow mines it’s usually energy that’s your problem, but in the deeper mines you want to keep your health bar full at all times.
Don’t let expensive stuff sit idle.
When you build a barn or a coop, you’ll have to visit Marnie to buy some animals. So do that. Don’t scrape for ages to get a barn big enough for 12 pigs - buy cows in the meantime. Happy animals can actually be sold for a small profit. If you have kegs and your expensive fruit won’t be ready for a few days, see if you can chuck in something quick like honey, hops or wheat. Not that kegs are particularly expensive.
Don’t buy cosmetic items in your first year.
2000-4000 gp is a lot for a Rarecrow, when you can just make a normal Scarecrow from the weeds and scrap on your farm. Leave it until the money is of cosmetic significance to you. Opportunities to collect the Rarecrows will recur.
Don’t sell seeds you just bought…
…or buy produce you just sold. Dreadful waste of money. Not that small amounts will set you back very much. Like many games, the storekeepers believe in Profit.
Don’t sell stuff you still need.
It’s hard to buy back produce you just sold - Pierre won’t add it to his stock unless there’s a lot of it - so take care when selling directly to him; one click and it’s gone! Also be careful before putting stuff in the shipping crate. At least the shipping crate will let you retrieve the last item you put in.

sections.title: Overview
sections.content_html: Stardew Valley has two minigames, both of which are accessed from the arcade machines at the Saloon. Beating either game will result in you getting your very own arcade machine to play them any time you want. To exit either game, press Escape or the corresponding button on your controller.

Beating either game will result in you getting your very own arcade machine to play them any time you want. To exit either game, press Escape or the corresponding button on your controller.

sections.title: Journey of the Prairie King
sections.content_html: This minigame is available whenever the saloon is open. The first level can also be played during one of the friendship events. If you beat the game, you can continue to play in Hard Mode until you run out of lives. See here for more details.
sections.content_text: This minigame is available whenever the saloon is open. The first level can also be played during one of the friendship events. If you beat the game, you can continue to play in Hard Mode until you run out of lives. See here for more details.

sections.title: Junimo Kart
sections.content_html: To unlock Junimo Kart, you will need the Skull Key from the bottom of the mines. The kart will move forward automatically. Your only control is left-clicking to make the kart jump. The duration of the click determines the height of the jump. Holes and rail stops will cause you to lose a life if you do not jump over them. Progress Mode has six levels to complete. When you finish a level, your lives will refill and the speed will increase. If you lose all your lives, you will be returned to the first level. Endless Mode has no flat areas between levels, so you can keep your rhythm up.

sections.group_title: Stardew Valley/Journey of the Prairie King
sections.title: Controls
sections.content_html: WASD moves the character. The arrow keys shoot. Holding two buttons at once will result in diagonal movement or firing. Diagonal shots are often the key to survival. Holding down the fire buttons will result in continuous firing. The spacebar will use the currently stored item.

Holding down the fire buttons will result in continuous firing. The spacebar will use the currently stored item.

sections.group_title: Stardew Valley/Journey of the Prairie King
sections.title: Items
sections.content_html:
Items drop randomly from enemies. The first item collected (other than coins and extra lives) will be put in the item slot on the top left until you are ready to use it. You will not drop it on death. Any additional items will be used immediately.

  • 1 Coin: Gives you one coin.
  • 5 Coin: Gives you five coins.
  • Extra Life: Increases your spare lives by one.
  • Coffee: Increases your speed for a limited time. Usually not worth the risk.
  • Heavy Machine Gun: Drastically increases fire rate for a limited time. Looks like an ammunition belt.
  • Nuke: Kills all on screen enemies without dropping any items.
  • Sheriff Badge: Combines the effects of Coffee, Heavy Machine Gun, and Shotgun. It lasts longer than most timed items.
  • Shotgun: Makes you fire three shots at once at a slightly lower rate for a limited time.
  • Smoke Bomb: Causes you to teleport to another location. Enemies will be confused and not move or damage you for a limited time, but will still spawn.
  • Tombstone: Turns you into a zombie. You can move faster and kill enemies on contact until the music stops.
  • Wheel: Makes you shoot in all eight directions at once for a limited time.

If you want use the stored item as an emergency device, it is best to use a Nuke or Wheel. Sheriff Badges, Smoke Bombs, and Tombstones are also useful.

sections.group_title: Stardew Valley/Journey of the Prairie King
sections.title: Stage 1
sections.content_html:
Area 1 has no cover and the only enemy that spawns is the Orc. Orcs have 1 HP, move at varying speeds, and sometimes don't even follow you. They will try to swarm you. Area 2 adds Spikeballs and stockades. Spikeballs initially have 2 HP and move very quickly, but they do not follow you. Once they deploy, they will have 6 HP and block Orcs. The stockades will block bullets and movement, so you can hide behind them if necessary. Once Area 2 is complete, you will have the option to buy an upgrade from the vendor. If you have 15 or more coins, you should buy the Ammo to double the damage your bullets do. If you have 10-14 coins, you should buy the Gun to increase your firing speed. The Boots increase movement speed, but they are generally a waste of coins until you get to Hard Mode.

Area 3 adds Ogres. Ogres have 3 HP, but move slowly. They will destroy deployed Spikeballs on contact. The stockades are now directly in the firing path to the spawn areas, so you will have to move around a bit more to shoot the enemies. Area 4 makes the stockade look like a fort. You should stay inside unless you can get to an item without dying. If you do not have the first Ammo upgrade yet, now is the time to buy it. If you do have it, but you do not have the 30 coins for the next Ammo upgrade, buy the Gun.

The Cowboy

The Cowbow has two basic movement patterns that he uses in a random order. One pattern will make him stay directly below you while he fires. You should be firing continuously just to the edge of his stockade. Dodge back in after your first bullet hits him. The other pattern has him move to one side, back to the center, and possibly to the other side, still firing continuously. He will then pause. When he performs this move, shoot him diagonally from the side he is not on. If he pauses in the open, you can fire straight down without worrying about counter attack. Usually it is easier to keep shooting diagonally. If you fail to hit him for an extended period of time, he will start firing diagonally.

sections.group_title: Stardew Valley/Journey of the Prairie King
sections.title: Stage 2
sections.content_html:
Area 1 has trees that can provide cover in the corners. Trees do not block shots. Ogres return, but the Orcs and Spikeballs have been replaced with Mushrooms and Pixies. Mushrooms have 2 HP and move very quickly, so they are tough to take down if you do not have the Ammo upgrade. Pixies have one HP and can fly over obstacles. They also spawn anywhere on the edge of the screen, so you will need to watch for them if you are hiding in a corner. After completing the area, you will get another chance to buy an upgrade. If you can afford the green Ammo, buy it to raise bullet damage to 3. Otherwise, upgrade your gun.

Area 2 has scattered trees and stumps. Stumps act like the stockades. You will effectively be focusing on three directions and sniping to the right when necessary. Area 3 has two streams with three bridges each. You will generally want to stay between the streams unless an item is beyond them. If you decided to buy the Boots, they will help you reach the item and get back quickly. After clearing the area, the vendor will come back. You are going to want the green Ammo for the next stage if you can afford it. If you already bought the green Ammo, a gun upgrade is better than the silver Ammo (which boosts bullet damage to 4). After choosing an upgrade, you will fight the Cowboy again. The fight is essentially the same as the first one.
sections.content_text: Area 1 has trees that can provide cover in the corners. Trees do not block shots. Ogres return, but the Orcs and Spikeballs have been replaced with Mushrooms and Pixies. Mushrooms have 2 HP and move very quickly, so they are tough to take down if you do not have the Ammo upgrade. Pixies have one HP and can fly over obstacles. They also spawn anywhere on the edge of the screen, so you will need to watch for them if you are hiding in a corner. After completing the area, you will get another chance to buy an upgrade. If you can afford the green Ammo, buy it to raise bullet damage to 3. Otherwise, upgrade your gun. Area 2 has scattered trees and stumps. Stumps act like the stockades. You will effectively be focusing on three directions and sniping to the right when necessary. Area 3 has two streams with three bridges each. You will generally want to stay between the streams unless an item is beyond them. If you decided to buy the Boots, they will help you reach the item and get back quickly. After clearing the area, the vendor will come back. You are going to want the green Ammo for the next stage if you can afford it. If you already bought the green Ammo, a gun upgrade is better than the silver Ammo (which boosts bullet damage to 4). After choosing an upgrade, you will fight the Cowboy again. The fight is essentially the same as the first one.

sections.group_title: Stardew Valley/Journey of the Prairie King
sections.title: Stage 3
sections.content_html:
Area 1 has Imps and Mummies instead of the previous stage's enemies. Mummies have 6 HP but move very slowly. Imps have 3 HP and fly very quickly. Focus on shooting the Imps. The tombstones act like trees. When the vendor arrives, buy either the green Ammo or the next gun upgrade. Ideally, you should now have bought three guns and two boxes of ammo, but the coin drops do not always permit that.

Area 2 has lava at the top and bottom edges. It will not hurt you, but it will prevent you from collecting any items that drop beyond it. The four tombstones are less helpful than Stage 1, Area 4's stockade, but they do provide some protection. Area 3 will only spawn Mummies on the left and right. This makes it hard to use the Mummies as protection against the swarms of Imps that spawn. Expect to lose quite a few lives here if you do not have the green Ammo. If you have the opportunity, replace your emergency item with a Sheriff Badge. Once the area is clear, the vendor will come back. If you have already purchased three guns, the gun slot will have a Sheriff Badge for 10 coins. If you do not have one in your item slot, use your current item and buy the Sheriff Badge. You can also get a Sheriff Badge if you have bought all three boxes of ammo. If you bought both pairs of Boots, you can get an extra life for 10 coins.

Fector

Fector can shoot in eight directions at once (from time to time), vary his firing speed, and spawn enemies to protect himself. He occasionally pauses. If you do not have the Sheriff Badge, focus on dodging while firing in his direction. If you do have the badge, wait until Fector is in the center of the area and you are in a corner. (Not the very corner, but a few squares away.) Use the badge and fire at him. Come closer if your outside shots are missing the enemies that he will try to spawn. This should destroy most of his health bar, if not all of it.

You can get similar results with a Heavy Machine Gun, but you will have to aim more. If you have a Shotgun, you can use the outside shots to hit Fector while he is doing his fire-in-eight-directions attack. If you brought a Nuke or Tombstone, it will only be useful against the extra enemies that Fector spawns. Touching Fector while in zombie mode may cause the game to become unwinnable. Coffee can help you dodge, but you should only be carrying it if you could not find a better replacement for your emergency item. Smoke Bombs may give you a short time to attack or a quick get away, but the random re-spawn location will limit your ability to get in shots. The Wheel item is virtually useless since the enemies will always be clumped in one spot.

sections.group_title: Stardew Valley/Journey of the Prairie King
sections.title: Hard Mode
sections.content_html: Once you beat Fector and watch the cutscene, you will be able to continue to Hard Mode with all your items and coins, but with three extra lives regardless of how many you had before. Extra lives will drop less frequently, so you may find that buying the Boots to get to the extra lives from the Vendor pays off. All enemies now have more HP. For example, Orcs will have 3 and Imps will have 5. Imps also spawn in every non-boss area. If you can survive long enough to collect 99 coins and all three gun upgrades, you will have the option to buy a Super Gun that will give you the three bullets of the Shotgun without the decrease in firing speed.

sections.content_html:
Legacy:Guide:Walkthrough [discuss]
Finally start to clean up this page by removing information from versions almost 10 years old. This is a Guide page.
enemy boss
Subject to revision (This Guide does not meet certain quality standards and may be heavily outdated.)
  • Issues:
    • Most likely outdated since 1.4.
    • Please do not use this guide. It has not been updated since 1.4 (not much), and it is contradictory. Remember not to delete pre-1.4 content; move it to Legacy:Guide:Walkthrough instead!
    Things to do:
    • General review.
    • Add Old One's Army sections.
    • Guide:Game progression Getting Started Guide.

    When progressing through Terraria, many players can be confused about where they should go and what they should do next. Terraria is an open-ended game: Players are not forced to go anywhere or do anything. You are free to set your own goals and follow through with them, whether you are a builder, fighter, explorer, collector, or whatever else. This walkthrough merely aims to provide a logical order of progression through Terraria's many different biomes, generally in order of increasing difficulty. It is recommended, but there is certainly no requirement to visit each biome, or even in this order if you don't want to.

    When choosing a map size, consider what experience you want out of your playthrough. A small world allows for quick exploration and easier traversal of difficult biomes early on, but can also feel limited, and may be missing certain rare items. A medium world allows for longer exploration and will have more items overall, but difficult biomes will be harder to traverse early on. A large world is best suited for multiplayer, or as a world that you intend to spend a lot of time on.

sections.title: Starting Out
sections.content_html:
On the creation of a new world, a helpful NPC (Non Player Character) will spawn, and he is called the Guide. If you are new to Terraria, then chat with him and he will give you advice on different elements of your world based on what stage of the game you're at. He can also be shown any material, and tell the player of any crafting recipes that use that item. He'll also inform the player on how to make a house that NPCs will accept as a place to live in.

Forest

New players will almost always spawn in the Forest biome.

Starting equipment

  • Green Slime
  • Blue Slime
  • Purple Slime
  • Cloud Slime(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions)
  • Pinky(rare)
  • Goblin Scout(only on outer thirds of world)
  • Gel
  • Cloud
  • Pink Gel(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions)(rare)
  • Slime Staff(extremely rare)
  • Tattered Cloth
  • Wood
  • Mushroom
  • Yellow Marigold
  • Sunflower
  • Daybloom
  • Blue Berries
  • Seed(from mining grass with Blowpipe in inventory)
  • Hay(from mining grass with Sickle)
  • Pumpkin(Halloween only)
  • Blowpipe
  • Grenade
  • Shuriken
  • Spear
  • Throwing Knife
  • Umbrella
  • Wand of Sparking(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions)
  • Wooden Arrow
  • Wooden Boomerang
  • Finch Staff(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions)
  • Aglet
  • Climbing Claws
  • Guide to Plant Fiber Cordage(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions)
  • Radar(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions)
  • Step Stool(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions)
  • Can Of Worms(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions)
  • Herb Bag(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions)
  • Glowstick
  • Rope
  • Torch
  • Bottle
  • Wood
  • Copper Bar
  • Tin Bar
  • Iron Bar
  • Lead Bar
  • Lesser Healing Potion
  • Recall Potion
  • Builder Potion(Desktop, Console, Old-gen console and Mobile versions)
  • Ironskin Potion
  • Mining Potion(Desktop, Console, Old-gen console and Mobile versions)
  • Night Owl Potion
  • Shine Potion
  • Swiftness Potion
  • Sunflower Minecart(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions)
  • Ladybug Minecart(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions)
  • Wood

The landscape of a forest includes lots of grass, plenty of trees, several lakes ranging from small to large and, sometimes, Sunflowers. During the day, this biome has the weakest monsters in the game, with slow weak slimes that jump towards the player being the primary threat. Note that Goblin Scouts only spawn in the outer thirds of the map, and as such will not be encountered in the forest you start in, but can be found in other forest biomes you happen to find.

Towards the entrance of caves you'll occasionally find Surface Chests, which can contain some of the above weapons, accessories, wood, metal bars, as well as various consumables. You can also run into Living Trees, massive trees made of solid blocks, which can lead underground and contain rooms with the unique Living Wood Chests and Living Loom, as well as additional Surface Chests.

Beginning

Your goal during the day should be to find/make some better starting equipment from your surroundings and build a small house to pass the night safely. The Guide will explain how you can make a valid NPC housing. It might be wise to build multiple houses in advance to house later NPCs. NPCs will show up when you meet the conditions for them to move in (for instance the Merchant will arrive once you have collected 50 or more Silver coins), and will leave come nightfall if you haven't made them a place to stay (except for the Guide). Don't worry, they'll come back, they just wont stick around without a home. The Guide will give you hints as to how to get new NPCs to move in.

If you're playing Journey Mode(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions), you'll start out with some better equipment in addition to many more powers over your gameplay experience, ranging from time control to item duplication. These are further explained in the main Journey Mode article.

The first thing players should do is cut down several trees (using your Copper Axe, aim for the lowest block), as wood is needed for many things, then build a Work Bench. From there, craft a Wooden Sword, and perhaps a Wooden Bow, (alongside some Wooden Arrows, which players can soon upgrade to Flaming Arrows for extra damage) and some Wood armor.

Next, players should explore their surroundings. Use the Ropes you can find and Platforms you can craft to help get around your world. Ropes can be used to safely descend down further than you can build, as simply placing rope on existing rope will cause it to extend downward. Ropes can also be crafted into Rope Coils, which can be a convenient way to traverse underground for the time being. If you happen to find the Umbrella tool, it allows for slow falling, which is another way to easily descend long falls. There are usually some Chests and Pots near the entrances of caves, which will often contain useful weapons, potions and materials (listed in the above "Forest" section). You should mine and collect these chests after you fully loot them, as they offer additional storage space.

If you're lucky, you’ll find some of the more notable beginner weapons, such as the Wand of Sparking(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) or Spear. These weapons will outclass your starting gear, and can be very helpful early on. You'll also likely find Recall Potions, which allow you to teleport back to your spawn. If you run into the Snow biome, you can very easily upgrade The Wand of Sparking into the Wand of Frosting(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions), only requiring 99 Ice Torches, which can also be used to craft Frostburn Arrows for your bow. Additionally, Snowballs can be crafted for an easy source of damage. You may also run into your Evil biome, which currently will be quite dangerous to you, so it's probably a good idea to simply Recall Potion or run away at the sight of an enemy. However, while you certainly shouldn't explore them at this point, you can swiftly chop (or bomb, which can clear trees faster) a couple trees down before recalling away and use the wood to craft either the Shadewood Sword and Shadewood Bow, or Ebonwood Sword and Ebonwood Bow for a quick and easy upgrade to your wooden weapons.

While exploring cave entrances, be sure to gather at least 20 stone, as combining it with some wood and torches allows you to craft a Furnace, which is required to smelt ores into bars. You can also use 5 bars of Iron or Lead to craft an Anvil, which is required to make most metal items. Alternatively, an anvil can be purchased from the Merchant. These two, along with your Work Bench, will be the 3 primary crafting stations you use to make the vast majority of items at this stage of the game.

After a little over 11 minutes, night will arrive. If possible, it's much more productive to head underground during the night, but if you perish or simply cannot make it to a cave in time, you can wait the night out if you like.


Night

9 in-game hours (9 real minutes)

  • Wooden Bow(with Flaming Arrows),
  • Spear,
  • Throwing Knife,
  • Shuriken
  • Grenade
  • Wand of Sparking(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions)(Can be upgraded to Wand of Frosting(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions))
  • Wooden Sword
  • Demon Eye
  • Zombie
  • Raven(Halloween only)
  • Lens
  • Shackle
  • Zombie Arm
  • Wooden Arrow
  • Black Lens
  • Fallen Star

Night falls at 7:30 PM, exactly 11 minutes and 15 seconds after you enter your world for the first time. It is signified by a change in music. Slimes will stop spawning and those that are left from the daytime will become hostile, seeking out players to attack. In addition, two new enemies will spawn: Demon Eyes, a flying enemy which chases players, and Zombies, which will follow a basic pattern of slowly walking towards the player in hordes.

Night has multiple effects on gameplay:

  • Fallen Stars will randomly fall from the sky with a glowing animation, and can be picked up by the player and crafted into a variety of things. Note that these disappear after sunrise.
  • Moonglow will bloom.
  • Some Town NPCs only sell certain items at night, such as the Merchant selling Glowsticks.
  • Town NPCs will remain in their houses and no new ones will move in until day arrives.

Two additional peaceful events can occur at Night. The starfall has a 1 in 10 chance of occurring each night and can be identified by stars being seen falling in the background. It's accompanied by an increased Fallen Star rate ranging from a 200% to 400% increase, as well as naturally spawning Enchanted Nightcrawler(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) critters, which make for great bait early on (caught with a bug Net bought from the Merchant). Lantern Nights, which feature lanterns floating up into the sky in the background, will also occur the night after defeating a boss or event for the first time, increasing the player's Luck.

If you find yourself outside without a base to hide in or a cave to go down, you can simply build a box around yourself to hide for the night. A two-block wide hole on either side of the box should be enough for you to attack Zombies and gain some starter gear and money, but you can also simply choose to dig straight down, blocking the entrance of the hole to prevent zombies from following, and continuing to dig hoping to run into a cave so you can spend the night mining, as it's much more productive.

As a relevant sidenote: If you're not used to playing Sandbox building/mining games, it is easy to forget your greatest ability: the power to manipulate your environment and move or destroy blocks. If you're in a pickle, this can save you much more often than it can't.

Fallen Stars are some of the most useful crafting materials at the beginning of the game. The most immediate weapon upgrade Fallen Stars make available is the Enchanted Boomerang, made with a single Fallen Star and a Wooden Boomerang. 5 Fallen Stars can be used to craft a Mana Crystal, which increases the player's maximum mana by 20 up to maximum attainable base mana of 200. This allows the player to use magic weapons for sustained periods of time, which can be very helpful if you found a Wand of Sparking(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions). They can also be turned into Jester's Arrows, arrows with high base damage that fly straight and pierce through crowds. Against single targets, both Flaming Arrows and Frostburn Arrows do more damage thanks to the debuffs they apply. They're also much cheaper. It's recommended you save Jester's Arrows specifically for large amounts of enemies at once, such as against crowds of Zombies or during events like the Blood Moon. Piercing weapons at this stage of the game are pretty rare, and if you find yourself in a situation where you need them and don't have them, it can easily create a problem, so try and save them if you can.

There are some valuable mob drops you can find at night. Zombies have a 2% chance of dropping the Shackle, which provides +1 defense. Shackles may also may spawn with a modifier, which grants an additional minor stat boost that can be useful. They can also drop the Zombie Arm, but only at a 0.4% chance. Demon Eyes will regularly drop the Lens, a crafting material which has a variety of uses.

Once the sun rises and morning arrives at 4:30 AM, Night will end, causing Demon Eyes and Zombies to flee and the day to begin once again. At this point you'll be able to explore the world more, so ideally your routine should be heading underground during night and exploring in the day until you become powerful enough to ignore the day and night cycle and traverse when you please.

A two-block wide hole on either side of the box should be enough for you to attack Zombies and gain some starter gear and money, but you can also simply choose to dig straight down, blocking the entrance of the hole to prevent zombies from following, and continuing to dig hoping to run into a cave so you can spend the night mining, as it's much more productive. As a relevant sidenote: If you're not used to playing Sandbox building/mining games, it is easy to forget your greatest ability: the power to manipulate your environment and move or destroy blocks. If you're in a pickle, this can save you much more often than it can't. Fallen Stars are some of the most useful crafting materials at the beginning of the game. The most immediate weapon upgrade Fallen Stars make available is the Enchanted Boomerang , made with a single Fallen Star and a Wooden Boomerang . 5 Fallen Stars can be used to craft a Mana Crystal , which increases the player's maximum mana by 20 up to maximum attainable base mana of 200. This allows the player to use magic weapons for sustained periods of time, which can be very helpful if you found a Wand of Sparking (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions). They can also be turned into Jester's Arrows , arrows with high base damage that fly straight and pierce through crowds. Against single targets, both Flaming Arrows and Frostburn Arrows do more damage thanks to the debuffs they apply. They're also much cheaper. It's recommended you save Jester's Arrows specifically for large amounts of enemies at once, such as against crowds of Zombies or during events like the Blood Moon . Piercing weapons at this stage of the game are pretty rare, and if you find yourself in a situation where you need them and don't have them, it can easily create a problem, so try and save them if you can. There are some valuable mob drops you can find at night. Zombies have a 2% chance of dropping the Shackle , which provides +1 defense. Shackles may also may spawn with a modifier , which grants an additional minor stat boost that can be useful. They can also drop the Zombie Arm , but only at a 0.4% chance. Demon Eyes will regularly drop the Lens , a crafting material which has a variety of uses . Once the sun rises and morning arrives at 4:30 AM, Night will end, causing Demon Eyes and Zombies to flee and the day to begin once again. At this point you'll be able to explore the world more, so ideally your routine should be heading underground during night and exploring in the day until you become powerful enough to ignore the day and night cycle and traverse when you please.

The Underground can be identified by its background and music. It is the first layer below the surface. Copper/Tin and Iron/Lead deposits can be found in this layer as well as Silver/Tungsten and Gold/Platinum, though infrequently.

The short depth of this layer (particularly on small worlds), combined with its limited rewards, means you will probably not be spending too much time here before moving on to the more lucrative Caverns. Copper/Tin is highly abundant, but players can easily skip them by farming cactus or ebon/shadewood equipment, or even simply going with nothing more than surface chest loot until they get enough Silver/Tungsten or Gold/Platinum that they can craft equipment out of that instead due to the former ores being notably weak. However, due to the lack of range and the slow speed of the Copper Pickaxe, it's likely worth investing in a Iron/Lead Pickaxe just for the increased efficiency.

While exploring the Underground (and, by extension, the Caverns), you might find Life Crystals: you can mine and use them to increase your maximum life by 20 (up to a maximum of 400). You can also stockpile Life Crystals and use them to craft Heart Lanterns, which increases life regeneration as long as you stay near to it. It's critical that you increase your max life, as it significantly boosts your survivability. That said, your first few crystals will also unlock various events: The first allows Blood Moons to happen, and event where spawnrates are greatly increased, and more powerful enemies spawn on the surface. The third allows Slime Rains, which causes slimes to fall from the sky. If you kill 150 slimes during this event, it causes the King Slime to spawn, who is the first boss. Using a fifth and getting up to 200 HP fufills one of the conditions for the Eye of Cthulhu to spawn naturally.

It is in this layer that the player can start to encounter Underground Cabins. These cabins will contain Golden Chests, which can contain a wide variety of useful equipment, such as Hermes Boots, which allow the player to run much more quickly, or a Cloud in a Bottle, which allows the player to double jump. Along with various potions and bars. These are the main things one should be looking out for during underground exploration.

Cavern

The Caverns can be identified by their background. It is the second layer below the surface and is by far the largest pre-hardmode biome. The Caverns are divided into two halves. In the top half, lakes of water are found, while in the bottom half, lava is found instead. Caves of Glowing Mushrooms can also be encountered.

The Caverns are a massive biome with many useful items and treasures, so they should be explored for a long time. The main things to be looking for are once again Underground Cabins, in addition to the now more common Gems and higher tier ores. The first gems the player finds should be used on making a grappling hook, as they greatly aid mobility. The player will also likely accrue a lot of money while down here, especially if they hold onto things they intention of selling them.

Although its monsters can be dangerous for a new player, the greatest threat in this layer may be the danger of falling into its deep chasms, frequently due to being hit by bats. Should you find yourself falling to death frequently, don’t forget there are a number of items that can break your fall: Cloud in a Bottle's (or equivalents) extra jump, Grappling any surface (with a Grappling Hook), including the ground you’re about to hit, or even an Umbrella. Pools of water (1+ block deep) and Cobwebs will also save you if you’re lucky enough to fall into them.

This ever-present danger is closely followed by the devious and near-invisible traps sprinkled throughout the dark caves. A bold, fearless new player skipping heedlessly through the caves for the first time will quickly meet with a Boulder landing on their head, a poison Dart Trap shooting at them, or a landmine powerful enough to destroy the surrounding terrain. Needless to say, tread with extreme caution, and take advantage of the Dangersense Potion(Desktop, Console, Old-gen console and Mobile versions). Upon spotting any trap or activating a Dart Trap, be sure to mine either the trap itself or the Pressure Plate. If one has no Dangersense Potions, they can also simply keep any item that uses wiring, such as the afformentioned Dart Traps or Pressure Plates in their Hotbar, as holding it will allow one to see wiring, which gives away where the traps are.

Of course, the easiest, and likely best method of avoiding the falls, the traps, and even the enemies is to use generous amounts of light sources. Torches are obviously the most common source of light, but there are alternatives. Items such as the Mining Helmet, Magiluminescence(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions), and Shine Potions, all provide light directly on top of the player, whereas items like the Flare Gun and Glowstick offer a source of ranged light. The former three provide supreme convenience, as with light constantly directly on top of you, you never have to worry about not being able to see, whereas the latter 2 can allow one to light up an area without having to approach. All of them also allow one to see underwater, where torches will not work.

While alternate light sources certainly can aid in easing exploration, all but the Magiluminescence(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) and the Mining Helmet are temporary, making torches still useful for revisited areas. The Mining Helmet, while permanent, is a weak gear choice and best replaced when acquiring a new set of armor for that armors set bonus. For those wanting to avoid placing torches, the Magiluminescence provides ample light, and unlike the Mining Helmet, is very useful and remains viable for much of the early game due to its acceleration bonus, a rare trait among mobility accessories. This acceleration boost is especially helpful in the tight Cavern spaces where other Movement Accessories, such as the Hermes Boots, struggle to build up speed. Even better, the Magiluminescence is craftable pre-boss with just 5 Topaz and 12 Demonite/Crimtane Bars (36 ore); the ore even glows, making it easy to find. It’s an excellent early-game upgrade, and if you're a new player struggling underground, crafting the Magiluminescence is highly recommended. The ore required to craft it is either purple (Demonite), or black and red (Crimtane). These ores require either bombs, or an upgraded pickaxe to mine (at least silver/tungsten). It is highly recommended to gather as much of these ores as you can, as they can also be used to craft powerful weapons like the Demon Bow or Blood Butcherer.

While exploring, the Skeleton Merchant(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) may show up. He sells a plethora of useful things, such as Glowsticks, Torches, Spelunker Glowsticks(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions), surface chest loot like the Wand of Sparking(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions), and Yoyo-related items such as the Red Counterweight(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions). He may also sell Roller Skates, a powerful mobility item. The roller skates allow the player to move extremely quickly, or slowly drift forwards, which is helpful for placing long rows of platforms. However, some players may find them awkward to use, due to their slippery controls.

Note that should you descend too far, you will actually find yourself in the Underworld. This will be marked by a change in music and background, along with the presence of Ash Blocks. The Underworld is extremely dangerous at this stage, and has nothing to offer yet aside from rare enemy drops.

There are many helpful tools to be found, ores to be mined, and resources to be collected in this layer. One of the first things to make is certainly a Grappling Hook simply because it is easy to craft thanks to Gem Hooks. Otherwise, the most important things to find are likely Life Crystals for reasons mentioned before, a pair of Hermes Boots, and a Cloud in a Bottle. The latter two, in conjunction with a Grappling hook and potentially a Magiluminescence(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions), serve the important purpose of bolstering mobility when it's very much needed. Another important find would be the Magic Mirror, which can substitute as an infinite form of the Recall Potion, so you no longer need to worry about running out.

It's important to note that all of the loot listed above that is found in chests (Hermes Boots, Cloud in a Bottle, Magic Mirror) can be found elsewhere. If you cannot find any of the above listed items in the caves below the forest you spawn in, you can simply explore left or right and find an equivalent (further explained in the "Beyond the Forest" section below).

In terms of weapons a player may want to craft a Gem Staff, an upgraded Bow or Broadsword, and if they afford it, weapons out of the Evil Biome ore. There are also various weapons that can be found in the caverns either in chests or as drops from enemies, such as the Shroomerang(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) and the Mace(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions).

A quick note on armor: Because of set bonuses, it is wise to try and complete an armor set rather than mixing and matching different pieces. Because of how Defense works, there isn’t a huge benefit from upgrading from one armor set to the next. The Copper armor set, for example, reduces damage taken by 3, Iron armor reduces damage by 5, so the difference in damage reduction is only 2, which is barely noticeable. Yet to complete the Iron armor set requires 225 ore, which represents a significant amount of mining time. It is therefore recommended to mine Silver or Tungsten Ore for the armor because they are good enough to take on the first bosses, are significantly faster to complete than Gold or Platinum, and allows you to save the latter for Weapons and Tools. If one is worried about the lack of defense, it should be noted that the damage reduction difference between the 4 different ores is practically negligible. The circumstance in which the difference is largest is on a world with both Silver and Platinum ore, as the Defense difference between the armors is a total of seven. Even in this circumstance, while it certainly could be beneficial to get the Platinum armor, it is still mostly unnecessary.

sections.title: Events
sections.content_html:
Events happen randomly as the player is traversing through the game, though some have certain criteria that need to be met in order to occur (for instance, a Blood Moon cannot occur until a player has at least 120 max health). Some events can also be summoned, and others can only be summoned and insetal will not occur randomly. These events can last either a full day/night, a random indeterminate amount of time, or will last until the player defeats them.


Rain

16.6% every day (approx. every six days)

24 in-game hours (24 real minutes)

  • Flying Fish
  • Umbrella Slime
  • Raincoat Zombie
  • Fries(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions)
  • Rain Song(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions)
  • Umbrella Hat
  • Rain Hat
  • Rain Coat

Rain occurs randomly and affects all surface biomes for its duration. Most enemies are only visually different from the normal enemies and behave exactly the same. The Flying Fish are the only one with any differences, but are still essentially a slower version of the Demon Eye. When a player is in a Snow biome during Rain, it appears as a Blizzard, though this doesn't provide any exclusive loot until Hardmode. If Rain happens at the same time as a Windy Day(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) it appears as a Thunderstorm(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) with exclusive music.

Effects of rain:

  • +20% Fishing Power while rain is active, regardless of location.
  • Waterleaf blooms, meaning mining it up will can also drop seeds which can be replanted.
  • Increased frequency of Worms in Forest biomes.
  • Town NPCs will remain in their houses as if it were night.
Windy Day

When wind reaches 20 miles per hour

Until wind drops to or below 16 miles per hour

  • Angry Dandelion(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions)
  • Windy Balloon(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions)
  • Daybloom
  • Paper Airplane(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions)
  • White Paper Airplane(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions)
  • Kites(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions)

Windy Days occur when the wind speed reaches over 20 miles per hour and end when it drops to or below 16. It is indicated by background objects such as banners, trees, and vines swaying in the direction of the wind, with upbeat background music replacing the regular music. Though the event is mostly aesthetic, with objects in the background and unique NPC quotes, there are some unique changes: Angry Dandelions(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) will sometimes spawn, firing dangerous dandelion seeds in the direction of the wind. They do heavy contact damage, but they can only attack to one side of them, making them easy to kill if the player is on the opposite side of the wind direction. Additionally, Slimes will spawn drifting on Windy Balloons. Slimes and a variety of other enemies have a small chance of dropping exclusive Kites(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) when this event is active, which can be flown in the wind.

Ladybugs(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions), used to craft Luck Potions(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions), spawn in clusters frequently near towns and are very useful to catch to make farming in the game easier. Touching them (before catching them) will also give an invisible but useful luck bonus for several minutes. Be warned not to accidentally kill them with stray projectiles, as they inflict a negative luck penalty on the player.

If Rain happens at the same time as a Windy Day it appears as a Thunderstorm with exclusive music and visuals. Thunderstorms also cause lightning strikes to occur. The area lightning is about to strike can be seen from sparks emitting from that location, touching these sparks will cause them to transfer to the player, causing lightning to strike them if shelter is not found quickly. Lightning will do high damage, and on higher difficulties may outright one shot the player if their health has not been upgraded enough.

Blood Moon

Given those criteria, 1 in 9 chance (11.11%) of occurring.

  • The Groom
  • The Bride(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions)

During a Blood Moon bunnies, goldfish, and penguins will turn hostile, and the spawn rate of all monsters on the surface will increase dramatically. Additionally, enemies will be able to spawn near NPCs and Zombies can force doors open.

Deathweed will bloom, and some NPCs will also sell special wares.

If you do not wish to fight in a Blood Moon, you should probably seek shelter underground where you will be beyond its effects. But with increased danger comes increased reward. The Shark Tooth Necklace(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) can drop from Blood Moon exclusive enemies, which increases armor penetration by 5, allowing the player to deal 2-3 extra damage to enemies with defense. The Money Trough(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) can also drop, which allows the player to summon a flying piggy bank whenever they want, which can be helpful if the player is running low on inventory space or suddenly comes across a large sum of money.

Guide:Blood Moon strategies
sections.content_text: Events happen randomly as the player is traversing through the game, though some have certain criteria that need to be met in order to occur (for instance, a Blood Moon cannot occur until a player has at least 120 max health). Some events can also be summoned, and others can only be summoned and insetal will not occur randomly. These events can last either a full day/night, a random indeterminate amount of time, or will last until the player defeats them. Rain 16.6% every day (approx. every six days) 24 in-game hours (24 real minutes) Flying Fish Umbrella Slime Raincoat Zombie Fries (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) Rain Song (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) Umbrella Hat Rain Hat Rain Coat Rain occurs randomly and affects all surface biomes for its duration. Most enemies are only visually different from the normal enemies and behave exactly the same. The Flying Fish are the only one with any differences, but are still essentially a slower version of the Demon Eye . When a player is in a Snow biome during Rain, it appears as a Blizzard, though this doesn't provide any exclusive loot until Hardmode . If Rain happens at the same time as a Windy Day (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) it appears as a Thunderstorm (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) with exclusive music . Effects of rain: +20% Fishing Power while rain is active, regardless of location. Waterleaf blooms, meaning mining it up will can also drop seeds which can be replanted. Increased frequency of Worms in Forest biomes. Town NPCs will remain in their houses as if it were night. Windy Day When wind reaches 20 miles per hour Until wind drops to or below 16 miles per hour Angry Dandelion (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) Windy Balloon (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) Daybloom Paper Airplane (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) White Paper Airplane (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) Kites (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) Windy Days occur when the wind speed reaches over 20 miles per hour and end when it drops to or below 16. It is indicated by background objects such as banners, trees, and vines swaying in the direction of the wind, with upbeat background music replacing the regular music. Though the event is mostly aesthetic, with objects in the background and unique NPC quotes, there are some unique changes: Angry Dandelions (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) will sometimes spawn, firing dangerous dandelion seeds in the direction of the wind. They do heavy contact damage, but they can only attack to one side of them, making them easy to kill if the player is on the opposite side of the wind direction. Additionally, Slimes will spawn drifting on Windy Balloons . Slimes and a variety of other enemies have a small chance of dropping exclusive Kites (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) when this event is active, which can be flown in the wind. Ladybugs (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions), used to craft Luck Potions (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions), spawn in clusters frequently near towns and are very useful to catch to make farming in the game easier. Touching them ( before catching them) will also give an invisible but useful luck bonus for several minutes. Be warned not to accidentally kill them with stray projectiles, as they inflict a negative luck penalty on the player. If Rain happens at the same time as a Windy Day it appears as a Thunderstorm with exclusive music and visuals. Thunderstorms also cause lightning strikes to occur. The area lightning is about to strike can be seen from sparks emitting from that location, touching these sparks will cause them to transfer to the player, causing lightning to strike them if shelter is not found quickly. Lightning will do high damage, and on higher difficulties may outright one shot the player if their health has not been upgraded enough. sections.title: Building a Base
sections.content_html:
Guide:Bases

Once you’ve filled your inventory with blocks and loot, you may want to consider starting to build a base, as now you have some building materials and money to buy things. A base can take anywhere from a single in-game day to more than an in-game week to complete, depending on the player's tastes. It is not necessary, however, to build the entire base right away. Waiting to build the majority of the base can be advantageous, as it will allow the player to use the large stores of blocks they will end up gathering as a by-product of mining. Regardless of when or what the player builds, it is recommended to build houses for the Guide, Merchant and Nurse, craft a Campfire, and an area for storage and crafting before progressing. It is also wise to create a layout that can be easily added onto later as more NPCs are available and more storage is needed.

You should have at least the following in your base before moving on:

  • Of course, houses for the Guide, Merchant and Nurse, as well as a valid empty house or two for other NPCs.
  • Several organized chests for item storage. You don't want to have a cluttered inventory every time you leave your base.
  • A campfire and sunflowers, both of which provide helpful buffs to those nearby. (Sunflowers also block the spread of Corruption and Crimson until hardmode, if you happen to have such biomes near your base.)
  • A crafting room, preferably with a chest or two in it to store crafting materials. Eventually, you're going to want a unified place for all your crafting needs. By now, you'll have a Work Bench, a Bottle on that Work Bench, a Chair next to it, a Furnace, an Iron/Lead Anvil, and probably a Sawmill and a Loom. A Chair and a Table adjacent to each other will serve as a crafting station for Watches. You should also leave some space for later-game crafting stations and more chests, but with just this setup, you'll be able to craft anything up to this point, from swords to robes to potions and building blocks.

If you die a lot, consider using the tombstones produced to make a flat, spread-out tree-free graveyard. If easily accessible early on it is a simple way to check regularly for Abigail's Flower which is a powerful early summon. The Ecto Mist in a graveyard is also needed to forge a Gravedigger's Shovel which can speed up digging immensely, as well as special blocks that could be useful for building interesting towns. Try to distance the graveyard slightly from the rest of the base area, as nighttime enemies can spawn at anytime in graveyards, as can other powerful enemies.

A Traveling Merchant will show up fairly early in game and sells many useful items, some of which are crucial for each class, such as the Gray Zapinator(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) and the Code 1(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions). He may also sell informational accessories like the Stopwatch(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions), DPS Meter(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) or Lifeform Analyzer(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions). Note that the merchant will despawn if you leave the game world and depart at 6:00 PM, so if you are far from him, you have to use a Recall Potion or leg it if you want the goods.

The Ice biome can be reached from the surface Snow, or from the Caverns, although sometimes there is no natural entrance from one or both. It ends where the lava layer begins.

The Snow biome is nearly identical to the Caverns in terms of difficulty; the only notable enemy to be woried about is the Spiked Ice Slime. It shoots a surprisingly accurate, high damage icicle projectile when in range, and if you get close to it, it will begin spewing many icicle projectiles at a shorter range, though it will stop for a moment if you hit it. Swords are a viable way to rid of these pests, but you'll need to get creative when approaching and approach quickly. A ranged weapon is much more effective though, and particularly Guns are most effective due to the projectiels fast speed making it difficult to miss. All other enemies can be dealth with trivially by simply swinging a sword at them; they will not be able to reach you.

Frozen Chests are slightly less common than Gold Chests and it can take a lot of exploring to find all the unique loot, though this process can be sped up with Spelunker potions. However, you should be wary of the thin ice pockets scattered throughout the biome to avoid a fall to your death.

Of the unique Ice Biome loot, the Flurry Boots are identical to the Hermes Boots and the Ice Mirror is identical to the Magic Mirror. The rest of the loot is very notable however, and is at least relatively useful.

  • The Blizzard in a Bottle is a strict upgrade to the Cloud in a Bottle; the double jump it provides grants more height. The bottles can both be equiped at once to allow for even more jumps.
  • The Ice Blade is a simple sword that shoots a projectile, and is better than any Ore Swords one can craft.
  • The Ice Skates themselves improve acceleration on Ice-related blocks quite a lot, and more importantly are a required crafting ingredient for upgrading your boots, so hold onto them.
  • The Snowball Cannon is a good, albeit replaceable, early game ranged weapon with high knockback.
Desert

Wooden Sword, Spear, Any thrown weapon ( )

The monsters in the Desert are weak and can be easily dealt with using ranged weapons, although Antlions, Vultures and (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) Antlion Swarmers may present a moderate challenge, they are rare to run into above ground. If you visit it, you can craft equipment from cactus, which is slightly stronger than Wooden equipment. (On (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions):) Cactus armor in particular gives a useful set bonus that causes the user to deal damage to enemies upon taking contact damage, similar to the Thorns Potion

One of the various desert will contain an entrance to the Underground Desert, which is typically wide, deep hole. (On (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions)) The entrance can also be smaller, ~1 block wide holes that if dug down will lead directly to the underground desert. Antlion Swarmers may try to fly out of the wide hole, as well as there being a risk of accidentally falling in; you can prevent both issues by building a bridge of solid blocks.

If you are lucky, Deserts may contain a Pyramid, though they're not guaranteed to spawn in any normal world (though they are guaranteed to spawn in Celebration worlds). They'll be found either sticking slightly out of the sand or buried just underneath. Items such as the Starfury and Jester's Arrows can allow one to look through the ground and potentially spot a buried Pyramid. Either entering the Pyramids entrance or digging through the Pyramid's sandstone walls will bring you to a chamber full of pots, coin bags, and a chest with unique loot. The chest may contain either a Flying Carpet, Sandstorm in a Bottle, both very useful accessories, or the Pharaoh's set, a vanity set. Previously, the worst of these three was undoubtedly the Pharaoh's Set, as it is purely decorative and serves no purpose, however as of version (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions)1.4.4.3, the Flying Carpet is actually the worst loot to be found. As of this update, the Pharaoh's Set can now be Transmuted into both the Flying Carpet and Sandstorm in a Bottle, and while the Flying Carpet is relatively useful, the Sandstorm in a Bottle is infinitely more so due to it being by far the best Double Jump accessory and being the hardest item to obtain for the extremely useful accessory Bundle of Balloons.

The Desert can also experience a unique event, a Sandstorm, in which Antlions are much more common, Tomb Crawlers can now spawn above ground, and the Sandstorm unique enemy Angry Tumbler(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) can now spawn. You are also permanently afflicted with the Mighty Wind debuff as long as you are in the Sandstorm. Due to the event providing no unique loot at this stage of the game, it's recommended you simply avoid the desert if a Sandstorm is occurring. It should (literally) blow over in about a day (8 minutes).

Underground Desert

At a minimum: Silver Broadsword or better, Gold Bow or better paired with Jester's, Bone(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions), or Frostburn Arrow's, an Emerald Staff or better, or a healthy amount of Throwing Knives.

Best choices: Light's Bane, Blade of Grass, Minishark, Vilethorn, Bone Throwing Knives(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions), and Grenades.

On (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions), the underground desert saw a massive overhaul, it's practically entirely different. As such, this section is broken into 2 parts: One for Modern versions, one for Old-gen-console.

Modern Console

Much like an actual bug nest, the Underground Desert swarms the player with enemies, namely the countless Antlion Chargers and Swarmers, but particularly Antlion Larva can easily get a jump on you due to the abundance of Antlion Eggs you can shatter. You'll rarely get a moment of peace outside of sealing yourself up with blocks, but even that can be risky thanks to Tomb Crawlers. You have to stay on your toes and ready to fight constantly; dipping anywhere below 40 health is extremely risky thanks to Tomb Crawlers and it's recommended you box yourself in to heal up.

The biome is deliberately generated in short but wide pockets, giving Antlion Chargers a unique advantage: speed. Antlion chargers are by far the fastest enemy in the game, and in wide areas they can blitz past you, dealing repetitive damage. It's still possible to stop them mid-charge, fast hitting weapons work best for this, such as the weapons labeled under the "Best" category in the above weapons section, but they're still dangerous regardless. This horizontal momentum can even give them extra jump height, allowing them to reach places that would otherwise be safe, so be weary. Despite this, the best strategy is definitely to be higher than them; their jump height isn't great and even though the Antlion Swarmers can fly, they are significantly less dangerous than the chargers and easily dealt with.

The most dangerous part of the Underground Desert is not the enemies. Instead, it's the Rolling Cactus(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions). It can deal as much as 200 damage to you, and can be triggered by projectiles, melee and pickaxe hits, and mining either it or the blocks below it. While they can also damage enemies, they take far less damage than you do. A ranged weapon and a Grapple makes clearing them out safe and easy, and it's highly recommended you do so. Stay clear of them as best you can, be sure to not fire blindly into new areas else you risk triggering one, and clear out the ones you see safely before moving forward.

A key and abundant resource here is the Desert Fossils(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions), which you can put through an Extractinator to get gems, ores, and coins, similar to Silt and Slush though with significantly more amber, as well as Sturdy Fossils(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions). Desert fossils are fragile, and crumble around a pickaxe -- bombs are the best method for harvesting them.

Should you manage to traverse the underground desert; a slew of great spoils awate you.

  • Sturdy Fossils(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) can be used to craft a lot of useful equipment:
    • Scarab Bombs(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions), great for effecient tunneling.
    • The Fossil Pickaxe(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions), a slightly faster but equivalent Platinum/Gold Pickaxe (though slower than the similar Bone Pickaxe).
    • Bone Throwing Knives(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions), an upgraded Throwing Knife which is great at handeling enemies in tight spaces, making it great for caving.
    • Bone Javelins(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions), which have a stacking damage overtime effect. A solid weapon for tanky enemies.
    • The Amber Staff(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions), the second best Gem Staff available.
    • Fossil armor(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions), a solid early-game ranger set.
  • The Thunder Zapper, the highest single target DPS of all early-game magic weapons, though it lacks piercing.
  • The Storm Spear, a very solid melee option.
  • The Ancient Chisel, boosts mining speed quite a bit and can be upgraded into a great utility accessory
  • The Magic Conch, allows you to teleport to either ocean instantly.
  • The Bast Statue, which offers a passive defense boost when placed in your arena.

The sandstone chests in the top 3/7ths of the biome can contain the Ancient Chisel(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions), Magic Conch(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions), Snake Charmer's Flute(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions), and Dunerider Boots(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) while the chests in the bottom 4/7ths of the biome can contain the Thunder Zapper(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions), Storm Spear(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions), and Bast Statue(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) so be sure that you are at the correct depth to be able to find the item you're looking for.

Oceans are always found at the edge of the world, usually next to beaches containing Palm Trees and decorative seashells and starfish. Water Chests are found typically in the deepest parts. New characters may have problems working in this biome because of sharks and a lack of air supply. Gills Potions can help in this regard.

This is also where you will find the Angler, who will help set you up for Fishing. (Old-gen console and 3DS versions) You will definitely want to do some fishing in this biome -- the varied loot can provide for a bit of money, and if you catch a Reaver Shark, you won't have to get a new pickaxe until Hardmode! On the  Desktop version,  Console version, and  Mobile version, it's not as powerful and is pretty slow as a pickaxe, so it's best to avoid it. The Sawtooth Shark is a decent chainsaw though.

For convenient fishing, set up a 30x10 lake near your base and/or pylons in Forest, Underground, Desert, Jungle, and Sky biomes. Having one near a base in the Forest will also give you a steady supply of Ducks for the Plenty Satisfied buff. Filling a lake can be done with a water-filled Bucket and placing blocks to duplicate the liquid.

The Corruption can be a challenging biome for players. Ebonstone can only be mined with a Nightmare Pickaxe, which can only be obtained after defeating the Eater of Worlds, but you can use Purification Powder, Bombs and/or Dynamite to destroy it before you’ve defeated the boss.

As soon as you think you can, it's recommended that you destroy 1-2 Shadow Orbs for you to obtain a Musket and another random item, as destroying the 3rd will summon the boss. This is surprisngly easy to do as soon as you obtain explosives and a way to cancel fall damage, as the enemies aren't hard to outrun. Movement accessories and a grappling hook should be all one needs to accomplish this. Outside of the shadow orbs, this biome doesn't provide much for the player until they can beat the biome-specific boss, so avoid it until then.

The Musket serves as a great early-game weapon, and more importantly it allows the Arms Dealer to move in, who sells ammo and an extremely good early-game weapon in the Minishark, though it's a bit pricey.

The Crimson is the other possible variant of the evil biome present in your world, instead of the Corruption. In general, the Crimson comtains slightly better loot as well as slightly stronger enemies. However, it is not a strictly "better" evil biome, as the Corruption provides some very useful items with no counterpart in the Crimson, like the Vilethorn, Worm Teeth (for Unholy Arrows), and the Band of Starpower.

Like the Corruption, there is practically no loot to be found here outside of breaking the Crimson Hearts and the biiome-specific boss. Once again it is not very difficult to break these hearts as soon as the player has explosives, some movement accessories, and any way to cancel fall damage. Break up to two crimson hearts so as soon as you think you can.

Cave generation is different to the Corruption: instead of deep shafts, it contains one big neuron-shaped cave that you can walk down more easily. If the Crimson presents in your world, Crimtane replaces natural Demonite spawns, and bosses would drop Crimtane as well.

Crimstone can only be mined with a Deathbringer Pickaxe or better, which can only be obtained after defeating the Brain of Cthulhu, but you can use Purification Powder, Bombs and/or Dynamite to destroy it before defeating the boss. It's recommended that you destroy 2 crimson hearts (but not the third) to obtain The Undertaker and another 1 of the 5 possible items, as destroying the 3rd will summon the boss.

Much like the Musket, The Undertaker allows the Arms Dealer to move in, which is again useful in obtaining the great but pricy [Minishark. The Undertaker itself however, is rather lackluster compared to the Musket. While certainly a good option as a weapon, it finds itself becoming obsolete relatively quickly, whereas the Musket can be useful for quite a while.

The jungle is one of the more difficult surface biomes due to the above ground Jungle Bats and plenty of Pihranha infested waters to slow the player down. It's still easy to traverse, but requires a bit more equipment than other surface biomes.

Important Disclaimer: The Underground Jungle is one of the most dangerous Pre-Hardmode areas, second to the dungeon and roughly equivalent to the Underworld. You should venture to the underground Jungle after exploring the Underground Desert or Ice Biomes, or both. That said, it’s also one of the most rewarding, offering some of the best gear available in early Pre-Hardmode, as well as plenty of accessories that are needed for future upgrades. If you can defeat the Eye of Cthulhu fairly easily, you’re more than likely ready to brave the Jungle, but you'll want to play cautiously. If you’re dying frequently or feel overwhelmed, leaving and coming back later is a wise decision, just don’t put it off for too long.

The Underground Jungle lies directly below the surface Jungle, beginning at variable depths, and extends to the Underworld. It also contains multiple Bee Hives and a Jungle Temple, which can not be entered until Hardmode, although Temple enemies, like the Lihzahrd, may spawn, if the player is standing in front of Temple Walls.

The primary threats in the Underground Jungle are the Hornet, which flies, attacks from range, and generally keeps its distance, and the Spiked Jungle Slime, which can launch venomous spikes at you from a surprisingly far distance. The easiest way to deal with these two enemies are with fast projectiles, which many of the recommended weapons have. Another very easy way to deal with them is to utilize blocks and hide, typically this is done by digging into/through the wall. You can then use weapons that allow you to hit them while they cannot hit you, such as Yoyos and the recommended Starfury. The Crimson Rod cannot be used through walls, but it can be set up and left to deal consistent damage to hornets as they fly around.

You may note that there are bigger, more open spaces than in the Caverns. This, in conjunction with the Jungles higher spawn rates, leads to swarms of hornets attacking from all directions which can be very dangerous. If you are using low-tier gear when first exploring it, it is much safer to stay to the side tunnels and the edges of the large caves until you've acquired better gear and more life.

Tunneling is especially safe in this area, unlike the Underground Desert, as the only enemy that can attack through walls that spawns in this area is the Man Eater, who is locked to a single position and can only extend so far. A patient player can easily traverse the jungle by tunneling and poking their head out when they see something they want, such as Jungle Spores or an easy to pick off enemy.

If you get a bit lucky, a hornet can drop a Bezoar, which is immensely helpful in dealing with the seemingly ever-present poison debuff every enemy applies. It's highly recommended to be equipped as soon as you find it, especially on higher difficulties where the debuff is applied for much longer periods of time.

Guide:Surviving in the Jungle

As stated, the Jungle is extremely lucrative, with the open spaces leading to a higher spawn rate of Life Crystals, the enemy drops being used to craft very powerful equipment, and the chests offering valuable unique loot.

The Stingers from Hornets & Spiked Jungle Slimes, Vines from Trappers, and Jungle Spores from the glowing spores found growing along the Underground Jungle Floor can be used to craft the following equipment:

  • Jungle armor: A very strong Mage set and the best available for Mages until Meteor armor (though Jungle armor does still outclass Meteor armor if one prefers not to use the Space Gun).
  • Blade of Grass: A phenomenal melee weapon available pre-boss with good reach and homing projectiles. Can later be upgraded into the very strong Night's Edge.
  • Thorn Chakram: The best boomerang available pre-boss, which also has the longest reach of all boomerangs and the ability to bounce multiple times.
  • Amazon(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions): The strongest yoyo pre-boss.

Outside of enemy drops, there's plenty of other unique loot found in both Underground Jungle chests and around the Jungle. The most notable finds are:

  • Feral Claws: These will increase your melee speed, and can prove very helpful later on in hardmode as they have multiple upgrades. Hold onto extras if you find them.
  • Anklet of the Wind: This considerably increases your movement speed and boots acceleration, and can also be combined at a Tinkerer's Workshop with Spectre Boots and an Aglet to make Lightning Boots.
  • Boomstick: By far the best gun available up until defeating Skeletron and overall one of the best ranged weapons until then.
  • Bezoar: Immunity to poison is extremely useful while you're in the Underground Jungle, and this accessory is very helpful when coming up against Queen Bee. This accessory is also needed to craft the Ankh Charm later on.
  • Honey: This will give you a healing buff upon touching it and is therefore very useful in boss arenas. Consider bringing Buckets along to pick it up.

It ends where the lava layer begins. The Snow biome is nearly identical to the Caverns in terms of difficulty; the only notable enemy to be woried about is the Spiked Ice Slime . It shoots a surprisingly accurate, high damage icicle projectile when in range, and if you get close to it, it will begin spewing many icicle projectiles at a shorter range, though it will stop for a moment if you hit it. Swords are a viable way to rid of these pests, but you'll need to get creative when approaching and approach quickly. A ranged weapon is much more effective though, and particularly Guns are most effective due to the projectiels fast speed making it difficult to miss. All other enemies can be dealth with trivially by simply swinging a sword at them; they will not be able to reach you. Frozen Chests are slightly less common than Gold Chests and it can take a lot of exploring to find all the unique loot, though this process can be sped up with Spelunker potions. However, you should be wary of the thin ice pockets scattered throughout the biome to avoid a fall to your death. Of the unique Ice Biome loot, the Flurry Boots are identical to the Hermes Boots and the Ice Mirror is identical to the Magic Mirror. The rest of the loot is very notable however, and is at least relatively useful. The Blizzard in a Bottle is a strict upgrade to the Cloud in a Bottle; the double jump it provides grants more height. The bottles can both be equiped at once to allow for even more jumps. The Ice Blade is a simple sword that shoots a projectile, and is better than any Ore Swords one can craft. The Ice Skates themselves improve acceleration on Ice-related blocks quite a lot, and more importantly are a required crafting ingredient for upgrading your boots, so hold onto them. The Snowball Cannon is a good, albeit replaceable, early game ranged weapon with high knockback. The chest may contain either a Flying Carpet , Sandstorm in a Bottle , both very useful accessories, or the Pharaoh's set , a vanity set. Previously, the worst of these three was undoubtedly the Pharaoh's Set, as it is purely decorative and serves no purpose, however as of version (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) 1.4.4.3 , the Flying Carpet is actually the worst loot to be found. As of this update, the Pharaoh's Set can now be Transmuted into both the Flying Carpet and Sandstorm in a Bottle , and while the Flying Carpet is relatively useful, the Sandstorm in a Bottle is infinitely more so due to it being by far the best Double Jump accessory and being the hardest item to obtain for the extremely useful accessory Bundle of Balloons . The Desert can also experience a unique event, a Sandstorm , in which Antlions are much more common, Tomb Crawlers can now spawn above ground, and the Sandstorm unique enemy Angry Tumbler (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) can now spawn. You are also permanently afflicted with the Mighty Wind debuff as long as you are in the Sandstorm. Due to the event providing no unique loot at this stage of the game, it's recommended you simply avoid the desert if a Sandstorm is occurring. It should (literally) blow over in about a day (8 minutes).
