As such, this section is broken into 2 parts: One for Modern versions, one for Old-gen-console. Modern Console Much like an actual bug nest, the Underground Desert swarms the player with enemies, namely the countless Antlion Chargers and Swarmers , but particularly Antlion Larva can easily get a jump on you due to the abundance of Antlion Eggs you can shatter. You'll rarely get a moment of peace outside of sealing yourself up with blocks, but even that can be risky thanks to Tomb Crawlers . You have to stay on your toes and ready to fight constantly; dipping anywhere below 40 health is extremely risky thanks to Tomb Crawlers and it's recommended you box yourself in to heal up. The biome is deliberately generated in short but wide pockets, giving Antlion Chargers a unique advantage: speed. Antlion chargers are by far the fastest enemy in the game, and in wide areas they can blitz past you, dealing repetitive damage. It's still possible to stop them mid-charge, fast hitting weapons work best for this, such as the weapons labeled under the "Best" category in the above weapons section, but they're still dangerous regardless. This horizontal momentum can even give them extra jump height, allowing them to reach places that would otherwise be safe, so be weary. Despite this, the best strategy is definitely to be higher than them; their jump height isn't great and even though the Antlion Swarmers can fly, they are significantly less dangerous than the chargers and easily dealt with. The most dangerous part of the Underground Desert is not the enemies. Instead, it's the Rolling Cactus (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions). It can deal as much as 200 damage to you, and can be triggered by projectiles, melee and pickaxe hits, and mining either it or the blocks below it. While they can also damage enemies, they take far less damage than you do. A ranged weapon and a Grapple makes clearing them out safe and easy, and it's highly recommended you do so. Stay clear of them as best you can, be sure to not fire blindly into new areas else you risk triggering one, and clear out the ones you see safely before moving forward. A key and abundant resource here is the Desert Fossils (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions), which you can put through an Extractinator to get gems, ores, and coins, similar to Silt and Slush though with significantly more amber, as well as Sturdy Fossils (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions). Desert fossils are fragile, and crumble around a pickaxe -- bombs are the best method for harvesting them. Should you manage to traverse the underground desert; a slew of great spoils awate you. Sturdy Fossils (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) can be used to craft a lot of useful equipment: Scarab Bombs (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions), great for effecient tunneling. The Fossil Pickaxe (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions), a slightly faster but equivalent Platinum/Gold Pickaxe (though slower than the similar Bone Pickaxe ). Bone Throwing Knives (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions), an upgraded Throwing Knife which is great at handeling enemies in tight spaces, making it great for caving. Bone Javelins (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions), which have a stacking damage overtime effect. A solid weapon for tanky enemies. The Amber Staff (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions), the second best Gem Staff available. Fossil armor (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions), a solid early-game ranger set. The Thunder Zapper , the highest single target DPS of all early-game magic weapons, though it lacks piercing. The Storm Spear , a very solid melee option. The Ancient Chisel , boosts mining speed quite a bit and can be upgraded into a great utility accessory The Magic Conch , allows you to teleport to either ocean instantly. The Bast Statue , which offers a passive defense boost when placed in your arena. Guide:Goblin Army strategies Jungle Ebonwood or Shadewood Sword, Bow, Gem Staff Cactus, or Ebonwood or Shadewood Piranha Snatcher Jungle Bat Jungle Slime Zombie Demon Eye Doctor Bones Hook Robot Hat Compass (Desktop, Console, Old-gen console and Mobile versions) Depth Meter Gel Slime Staff Shackle Zombie Arm Wooden Arrow Archaeologist's Hat Moonglow Jungle Rose Jungle Grass Seeds Sky Blue Flower Rich Mahogany Double Cod Neon Tetra Jungle Crate (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) Do Not Step on the Grass The jungle is one of the more difficult surface biomes due to the above ground Jungle Bats and plenty of Pihranha infested waters to slow the player down. It's still easy to traverse, but requires a bit more equipment than other surface biomes. Important Disclaimer: The Underground Jungle is one of the most dangerous Pre-Hardmode areas, second to the dungeon and roughly equivalent to the Underworld. You should venture to the underground Jungle after exploring the Underground Desert or Ice Biomes, or both. That said, it’s also one of the most rewarding, offering some of the best gear available in early Pre-Hardmode, as well as plenty of accessories that are needed for future upgrades. If you can defeat the Eye of Cthulhu fairly easily, you’re more than likely ready to brave the Jungle, but you'll want to play cautiously. If you’re dying frequently or feel overwhelmed, leaving and coming back later is a wise decision, just don’t put it off for too long. Underground Jungle Starfury Malaise/Artery (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) Musket The Undertaker Minishark Snowball Cannon Thunder Zapper (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) High-tier Gemstaff Crimson Rod Silver/Tungsten Gold/Platinum Fossil (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) Shadow Crimson Meteor Molten Molten Fury Volcano Space Gun Flamarang Any double jump Lucky Horseshoe any Horseshoe Balloon Magiluminescence (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) Bezoar Hornet Man Eater Jungle Bat Piranha Spiked Jungle Slime Lac Beetle Doctor Bones Stinger Vine Hook Bezoar Violet Husk (Desktop, Console, Old-gen console and Mobile versions) Ancient Cobalt armor Archaeologist's Hat Moonglow Jungle Spores Jungle Rose Nature's Gift Sky Blue Flower Rich Mahogany Boomstick Staff of Regrowth Anklet of the Wind Feral Claws Flower Boots (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) Fiberglass Fishing Pole Seaweed Living Mahogany Wand (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) Rich Mahogany Leaf Wand (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) Honey Dispenser (Desktop, Console, Old-gen console and Mobile versions) The Underground Jungle lies directly below the surface Jungle, beginning at variable depths, and extends to the Underworld. It also contains multiple Bee Hives and a Jungle Temple , which can not be entered until Hardmode, although Temple enemies, like the Lihzahrd , may spawn, if the player is standing in front of Temple Walls. The primary threats in the Underground Jungle are the Hornet, which flies, attacks from range, and generally keeps its distance, and the Spiked Jungle Slime, which can launch venomous spikes at you from a surprisingly far distance. The easiest way to deal with these two enemies are with fast projectiles, which many of the recommended weapons have. Another very easy way to deal with them is to utilize blocks and hide, typically this is done by digging into/through the wall. You can then use weapons that allow you to hit them while they cannot hit you, such as Yoyos and the recommended Starfury . The Crimson Rod cannot be used through walls, but it can be set up and left to deal consistent damage to hornets as they fly around. You may note that there are bigger, more open spaces than in the Caverns. This, in conjunction with the Jungles higher spawn rates, leads to swarms of hornets attacking from all directions which can be very dangerous. If you are using low-tier gear when first exploring it, it is much safer to stay to the side tunnels and the edges of the large caves until you've acquired better gear and more life. Tunneling is especially safe in this area, unlike the Underground Desert , as the only enemy that can attack through walls that spawns in this area is the Man Eater , who is locked to a single position and can only extend so far. A patient player can easily traverse the jungle by tunneling and poking their head out when they see something they want, such as Jungle Spores or an easy to pick off enemy. If you get a bit lucky, a hornet can drop a Bezoar , which is immensely helpful in dealing with the seemingly ever-present poison debuff every enemy applies. It's highly recommended to be equipped as soon as you find it, especially on higher difficulties where the debuff is applied for much longer periods of time. Guide:Surviving in the Jungle As stated, the Jungle is extremely lucrative, with the open spaces leading to a higher spawn rate of Life Crystals , the enemy drops being used to craft very powerful equipment, and the chests offering valuable unique loot. The Stingers from Hornets & Spiked Jungle Slimes , Vines from Trappers , and Jungle Spores from the glowing spores found growing along the Underground Jungle Floor can be used to craft the following equipment: Jungle armor : A very strong Mage set and the best available for Mages until Meteor armor (though Jungle armor does still outclass Meteor armor if one prefers not to use the Space Gun). Blade of Grass : A phenomenal melee weapon available pre-boss with good reach and homing projectiles. Can later be upgraded into the very strong Night's Edge . Thorn Chakram : The best boomerang available pre-boss, which also has the longest reach of all boomerangs and the ability to bounce multiple times. Amazon (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions): The strongest yoyo pre-boss. Outside of enemy drops, there's plenty of other unique loot found in both Underground Jungle chests and around the Jungle. The most notable finds are: Feral Claws : These will increase your melee speed, and can prove very helpful later on in hardmode as they have multiple upgrades. Hold onto extras if you find them. Anklet of the Wind : This considerably increases your movement speed and boots acceleration, and can also be combined at a Tinkerer's Workshop with Spectre Boots and an Aglet to make Lightning Boots . Boomstick : By far the best gun available up until defeating Skeletron and overall one of the best ranged weapons until then. Bezoar : Immunity to poison is extremely useful while you're in the Underground Jungle, and this accessory is very helpful when coming up against Queen Bee. This accessory is also needed to craft the Ankh Charm later on. Honey : This will give you a healing buff upon touching it and is therefore very useful in boss arenas. Consider bringing Buckets along to pick it up.

sections.title: The Bosses: Dealing with the first three
sections.content_html:
Once you’ve survived the first couple nights and started work on a base, you should begin preparations for the upcoming boss battles, as even if you do not wish to go looking for them, they will come looking for you.

King Slime

Guide:King Slime strategies

King Slime is an entirely optional but fun boss: none of its drops are necessary for game advancement.

King Slime can spawn rarely in Grass at the outer sixth of the world, by using a Slime Crown, or during a Slime Rain if the player kills 150 slimes (75 if King Slime has already been defeated). As with all monsters that can spawn naturally, the King Slime has a better chance of spawning while standing near a placed Water Candle or under the effects of a Battle Potion. It's extremely unlikely you will ever come across King Slime without planning to. King Slime is a good challenge for a beginning player and can be easily defeated by tactical use of terrain.

Still, savvy players may want to defeat King Slime for the chance of getting a good Slime Hook(Desktop, Console, Old-gen console and Mobile versions), as it's better than any hook obtainable up to this point. In the  Desktop version,  Console version, and  Mobile version, the Ninja armor it drops provides critical hit bonuses, useful for all weapons except summoning weapons, which aren't affected by critical hits. It also drops the Slimy Saddle(Desktop, Console, Old-gen console and Mobile versions), a mount with a fast fall speed that is useful for dodging in boss fights even into Hardmode.

Eye of Cthulhu

Guide:Eye of Cthulhu strategies

Although not required, the Eye of Cthulhu can be a beneficial boss to fight, providing Demonite or Crimtane Ore without the need to mine for the respective ore.

The Eye of Cthulhu takes the form of an enormous Demon Eye. His fight is composed of two phases. During the first phase, he spawns Servants of Cthulhu while hovering over the player. After spawning a few Servants of Cthulhu, he will make a series of three charges towards the player before repeating this process. When the Eye’s health falls below half (or 65% at Expert/Master mode), he transforms into his second phase. In this second phase, the Eye of Cthulhu no longer spawns Servants, but in turn follows the player more aggressively. His defense is also lowered in this phase, speeding up the fight as his health depletes faster.

In Expert Mode, as the Eye of Cthulhu's health is drained in his second phase, he gains the ability to perform a chain of swift charges toward the player, which eventually replace his standard charges at low health. As his health is drained further, the chain of charges grows longer while decreasing the time interval between each chain. With a sliver of health left, the Eye of Cthulhu enters a state of permanent charging, making constant short lunges at the player.

Eater of Worlds or Brain of Cthulhu

After the Eye of Cthulhu is defeated, you should do the following:

  • Be sure the Dryad has a home: she sells Purification Powder, a less explosive option for getting to the Shadow Orbs and Crimson Hearts, and planters, a more convenient way to grow your plants.
  • Make sure to have at least 12 valid NPC houses and be sure you can access them without having to walk or ride a minecart all the way across the map. One way to do this is to have them linked by (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) Pylons.
  • Start on your herb farm: Potions will be immeasurably helpful throughout the rest of the game.
  • Build a chest room: It's not a bad idea to have plenty of storage to put away items you'll find later on.

After this, head to the Corruption or Crimson to smash a Shadow Orb or Crimson Heart. Smashing your first orb or heart allows (Old-gen console and 3DS versions) two events/ (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) 1 event to occur in short order:

Meteorite

50% on (Old-gen console and 3DS versions) breaking a Shadow Orb or Crimson Heart (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) defeating the Eater of Worlds/Brain of Cthulhu

Vilethorn

Silver/Tungsten

Dynamite, Sticky Bombs, Gold or Platinum Pickaxe, buff potions

  • Meteor Head
  • Meteorite

(Old-gen console and 3DS versions) Smashing an orb/heart (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) Defeating the Eater of Worlds/Brain of Cthulhu will give a 50% chance for a meteorite to land the next night, (Old-gen console and 3DS versions) smashing additional orb/hearts (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) defeating additional Eaters of Worlds/Brains of Cthulhu after the first one on the same day will not increase your chance of a meteorite landing. However, if it is between midnight and dawn (04:30), the meteorite may land immediately. Meteorite mining can be challenging. You will be constantly harassed by the Meteor Heads, and touching any part of what you are trying to mine will burn you. An Obsidian Skull can prevent this damage. Mining with a pickaxe is slow, tedious, and frustrating.

(Old-gen console and 3DS versions) The Dynamite or Bomb is perfect with a large blast radius. You can build a wood platform over the middle of the crater to make it easier to throw them as well as allowing you to easily deal with meteor heads coming from below. You can then quickly clean up remaining sections with Sticky Bombs. Once there are fewer than 50 meteorite blocks in the area, it will cease to be a Meteorite biome and Meteor heads will no longer spawn.

On  Desktop,  Console, and  Mobile, the player can kill 50 meteor heads to obtain their banner, which makes it easier to deal with meteorite biomes.

Every third Orb or Heart you smash in the world will spawn either Eater of Worlds or Brain of Cthulhu respectively:

Eater of Worlds

Guide:Eater of Worlds strategies

Eater of Worlds is a worm boss 50 segments long , each with their own health. When a segment in the middle is destroyed, the two severed parts will each become new worms, each with their own head and tail. This boss must be fought in the Corruption, and will disappear if you leave it at any point during the fight.

You will not face an easier boss in Terraria than EoW, especially in melee. The reason for this is when you swing your melee weapon as the worm glides past, is running itself into your swing and damaging many segments, and rangers can use a demon bow and jester arrows for penetration,which is very useful, when Magic weapons at this point usually only hit 2-4 times per shot.

In Expert mode, you may not want to take the EoW aboveground because its damaging ranged attacks will no longer be frequently blocked if you do so.

Brain of Cthulhu

Guide:Brain of Cthulhu strategies

The Brain of Cthulhu is a boss that teleports and has two stages. In the first stage, it is invincible and surrounded by 20 Creepers. You must kill all the creepers before you can damage the Brain. In the second stage, you fight the Brain directly as it tries to charge you.

In Expert mode, when you reach its second phase, the Brain creates three fake copies of itself. The copies become more opaque as the Brain loses health.

sections.title: The Late Pre-Hardmode
sections.content_html:
The three late pre-hardmode biomes — the Underground Jungle, Dungeon, and Underworld — are all of the roughly similar difficulty and can be done in any order or concurrently.

The Underworld

The Underworld
  • Obsidian(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions)
  • Shadow
  • Crimson
  • Meteor

Lava Waders or Lava Charm, Water Walking Potion, Obsidian Skin Potion, Obsidian Skull or other obsidian accessory

  • Lava Slime
  • Hellbat
  • Fire Imp
  • Demon
  • Voodoo Demon
  • Bone Serpent
  • Demon Scythe
  • Obsidian Rose
  • Guide Voodoo Doll
  • Plumber's Hat
  • Magma Stone
  • Cascade(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions)
  • Hellstone
  • Fireblossom
  • Hellforge
  • Demon Torch
  • various Obsidian furniture
  • Dark Lance
  • Flower of Fire
  • Sunfury
  • Flamelash
  • Hellwing Bow(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions)
  • Treasure Magnet(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions)
  • Demonic Hellcart(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions)
  • Slice of Hell Cake(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions)
  • Ornate Shadow Key(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions)
Hotline Fishing Hook Lavaproof Fishing Hook bait
  • Flarefin Koi
  • Obsidifish
  • Obsidian Swordfish
  • Demon Conch(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions)
  • Bottomless Lava Bucket(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions)
  • Lava Absorbant Sponge(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions)
  • Obsidian Crate(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions)
  • Hellstone Crate(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions)(Hardmode)

The Underworld is found at the bottom of the world. The best items pre-hardmode can be found in or crafted from items found in this biome. Shadow Chests found here can only be opened with the Shadow Key, found in the Dungeon.

The Underworld is the hardest pre-hardmode biome, and the last biome that players explore.

The greatest danger working in the Underworld is, unsurprisingly, the wide expanses of molten lava. There are certain accessories which provide invaluable aid when it comes to traversing the Underworld, such as the Lava Waders and its upgrades, which allow walking on water. If you don't have these accessories, potions like Water Walking and Obsidian Skin are fantastic alternatives. When used, these potions allow you to walk on lava and become invulnerable to its damage respectively. There is no breath meter in lava, so as long as you have Obsidian Skin Potions, you can stay in lava indefinitely.

Guide:Surviving in the Underworld

Hellstone mining is quite time-consuming and is the main reason to spend time in it. You'll need an Obsidian Skull or better to prevent Hellstone ore and bricks from burning you. Abundant deposits of Hellstone spawn next to the buried Ruined Houses, and instead of going to burrow deep into the ash and build lava channels, mine the ones that spawn close to the walls. Monster spawn rates are low in the Ruined Houses, and the buildings prevent most of them from bothering you, except the Fire Imps and Bone Serpents which can penetrate blocks. You can block the Fire Imp shots with any weapon or projectile, including your swinging pickaxe.

Guide:Mining techniques § Mining Hellstone

Be mindful that if you kill a Voodoo Demon, you better be ready to get under that Guide Voodoo Doll before it drops into the lava, or you will be in for a nasty fight you're not prepared for. Should you accidentally awaken the Wall of Flesh, you cannot escape. Using a Magic Mirror will result in your death.

sections.title: Deerclops
sections.content_html:
Guide:Deerclops strategies

Deerclops is not especially difficult. The important things to note are that it becomes invincible if the player is more than 30 blocks away from it and that it doesn't despawn when the player dies, but rather when a full in-game day has passed from when it spawned (24 minutes).

It drops some good loot, but the main thing we want is the Houndius Shootius(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions). It's the first sentry available to the player, and will prove to be helpful in the upcoming event. Sentries are like minions, but they don't count towards the max minion count and are immobile. Every class should use at least one minion and one sentry as soon as they have them available, as there's no downside to using them.

sections.title: Old One's Army
sections.content_html:
Guide:Old One's Army strategies

The Old One's Army is an event that can be triggered after finding the Tavernkeep. The event focuses on defending the Eternia Crystal from the waves of enemies coming to attack it. To start the event, you must purchase an Eternia Crystal(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) and Eternia Crystal Stand(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) from the Tavernkeep. You must then build a decently sized flat arena, as the event will not start if the surrounding area is not flat enough. The Taverkeep will also give you free Defender Medals(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions), enough to purchase two sentries. It's highly recommended to purchase the Ballista Rod(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) and Lightning Aura Rod(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions). These are the two easiest to use and generally best sentries for the event.

The event has 5 waves of increasing difficulty. Enemies in this event drop a resource called Etherian Mana, this mana allows you to summon additional Tavernkeep sentries, costing 10 mana per sentry placed down. This mana disappears after the event, so don't try to save it. Any sentries not purchased from the Tavernkeep will work as they typically do in this event. Waves 1-3 are not very difficult, and should be used to set up defenses for the last two waves. On Wave 4 Etherian Wyverns begin to spawn, they're flying enemies that attempt to dive bomb the crystal. They need to be given priority over other enemies as they can evade the vast majority of sentry attacks and deal high damage if left unattended. On Wave 5 the Dark Mage spawns, the boss of the Old One's Army. It must be defeated for the event to end, so it needs to be given high priority. However, beware of focusing entirely on it, as the crystal could become overwhelmed while you're focusing on something else.

Every class should get summoner gear for this event, as the majority of your damage will be coming from sentries. Obsidian armor(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) is an exceptionally good choice, thanks to its ease of access and high damage boosts. The Imp Staff(Desktop, Console, Old-gen console and Mobile versions) will also be extremely helpful, and should be acquired before attempting the event. The Houndius Shootius(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) from Deerclops will also be helpful, as it will act as an extra sentry that doesn't cost Etherian Mana. Summoning Potions are handy, but not needed.

  • Melee players will want the Volcano for the Dark Mage and Wyverns. The explosion it causes also makes it exceptionally good against the hordes.
  • Rangers will want a Minishark or Boomstick for the Dark Mage and Wyverns. The Molten Fury with Jester's Arrows will also be very helpful for the crowds. The Star Cannon can be used if you're having a significant amount of trouble, but should be unnecessary.
  • Mages will want the Demon Scythe, it shreds through the crowds, Wyverns, and the Dark Mage extremely well. The Crimson Rod is also helpful as a minor source of extra damage.
  • Summoners will want the Snapthorn(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) in addition to the summoner gear already recommended by this guide.

You should start the event by placing a lightning aura sentry at one portal, try to get the max radius possible by aligning the edge of the sentry with the portal. As you get mana continue to place lightning aura sentries (make sure they don't overlap much) until the grounded enemies die just from the lightning aura. After this put down ballistas closer to the crystal to help get the Wyverns. When the Dark Mage spawns (you can tell because its healthbar appears on screen) place as many ballistas as possible near the crystal and go fight it, making sure to still keep watch of the crystal to make sure it doesn't die.

Upon clearing the event you will receive many benefits. You will be able to summon the Tavernkeep's Sentries outside of the Old One's Army event, which will help with the upcoming bosses. The Eternia Crystal will have dropped some Defender's Medals, which you should store away for safekeeping. The Dark Mage will have likely dropped an accessory, either the Squire's Shield(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) or Apprentice's Scarf(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) and a War Table(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions). Only one of the accessories is needed, as they offer the same boost and their boosts cannot stack. The accessories both give a 10% damage boost to summon weapons and an additional sentry slot. This is exceptionally helpful for summoners as this is a very large boost for a accessory to give this early. The War Table is helpful as interacting with it gives you a free buff that lasts until death, this buff allows you to summon an additional sentry.
sections.content_text: Guide:Old One's Army strategies The Old One's Army is an event that can be triggered after finding the Tavernkeep . The event focuses on defending the Eternia Crystal from the waves of enemies coming to attack it. To start the event, you must purchase an Eternia Crystal (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) and Eternia Crystal Stand (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) from the Tavernkeep. You must then build a decently sized flat arena, as the event will not start if the surrounding area is not flat enough. The Taverkeep will also give you free Defender Medals (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions), enough to purchase two sentries. It's highly recommended to purchase the Ballista Rod (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) and Lightning Aura Rod (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions). These are the two easiest to use and generally best sentries for the event. The event has 5 waves of increasing difficulty. Enemies in this event drop a resource called Etherian Mana, this mana allows you to summon additional Tavernkeep sentries, costing 10 mana per sentry placed down. This mana disappears after the event, so don't try to save it. Any sentries not purchased from the Tavernkeep will work as they typically do in this event. Waves 1-3 are not very difficult, and should be used to set up defenses for the last two waves. On Wave 4 Etherian Wyverns begin to spawn, they're flying enemies that attempt to dive bomb the crystal. They need to be given priority over other enemies as they can evade the vast majority of sentry attacks and deal high damage if left unattended. On Wave 5 the Dark Mage spawns, the boss of the Old One's Army. It must be defeated for the event to end, so it needs to be given high priority. However, beware of focusing entirely on it, as the crystal could become overwhelmed while you're focusing on something else. Every class should get summoner gear for this event, as the majority of your damage will be coming from sentries. Obsidian armor (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) is an exceptionally good choice, thanks to its ease of access and high damage boosts. The Imp Staff (Desktop, Console, Old-gen console and Mobile versions) will also be extremely helpful, and should be acquired before attempting the event. The Houndius Shootius (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) from Deerclops will also be helpful, as it will act as an extra sentry that doesn't cost Etherian Mana. Summoning Potions are handy, but not needed. Melee players will want the Volcano for the Dark Mage and Wyverns. The explosion it causes also makes it exceptionally good against the hordes. sections.title: Queen Bee
sections.content_html:
Guide:Queen Bee strategies

Queen Bee is not difficult to fight with at this stage in the game. Her charge attack is predictable and easy to dodge, and you can stand in the honey for a big healing boost.

Many of the Queen Bee's drops may be better than what you already have. Even if they aren't, farming Queen Bee is a good source of income before Hardmode. Plus, the Bee mount is the earliest mounts that can fly, although it's slow on land and hates water.

Skeletron is one of the most difficult pre-hardmode bosses, and is generally fought after Queen Bee. It consists of a head and 2 hands that fly around and follow the player.

The head has the most health of all the segments of Skeletron and when it is defeated, the player would kill the whole boss, regardless if there are hands or not. The head will float around the player for a few seconds and then start spinning and chasing down the player. This repeats for the whole fight.

The hands of Skeletron will mostly stay underneath the head, and will try to hit the player constantly. It is recommended to go for the hands first before fighting the head, especially in Expert and Master mode, where the head's defense will increase by 25 for the amount of hands that are remaining.

The Dungeon can be found near the right or left edge of the map, always on the opposite side of the Jungle and on the same side as the Snow biome. Note that attempting to enter the Dungeon before Skeletron is defeated will lead to an unpleasant surprise.

With its extremely high spawn rates, the abundance of dangerous traps, and general inability to use terrain as cover, even experienced players can be overwhelmed. If you find yourself overwhelmed by enemies, taking down every water candle you see will significantly reduce spawn rates (you may even want to use a Calming Potion). Certain room geometries can lead to a continuous stream of enemies spawning, generally rooms with large sections offscreen and multiple hallways leading into them. In these cases, it may be wise to move on as quickly as possible.

Guide:Surviving in the Dungeon

Make sure to get the following loot before leaving the Dungeon:

  • Shadow Key: This item can unlock any Shadow Chest in the Underworld. These chests contain many powerful weapons to use against and often still remain decent in early hardmode.
  • Cobalt Shield: Protection against knockback can be invaluable. The Cobalt Shield can also be tinkered with an Obsidian Skull to make an Obsidian Shield, which will prove very valuable in the Underworld as well.
  • Muramasa: This is one of the swords used to make the Night's Edge, which is the best sword and melee weapon before Hardmode.
  • Water Bolt: This weapon's piercing and bouncing projectiles can wreck any enemy in the Dungeon, Jungle, and Underworld.
  • Handgun: This weapon is a strong, reliable ranged weapon, provided you enable Autofire in settings. Can and should be upgraded into the more powerful Phoenix Blaster.
  • Nazar: Although not very useful outside the Dungeon, this accessory is needed to craft the Ankh Charm. It is highly recommended to farm for this accessory before unlocking the Hardmode dungeon, as the Cursed Skulls which drop it will become much rarer then.

sections.title: Preparing For Hardmode
sections.content_html:
At this point you have no deadlines or threats looming over you. You should be more-or-less the master of all you survey, and you have a wide variety of resources available. This is a good time to do large projects like arenas, bases, or farms, though you should keep in mind that depending on location, your base or arena might end up in an infected biome. You'll also need to collect some materials that will be needed in Hardmode, as farming is a lot easier in pre-Hardmode. You should also locate and construct a safe path to a Spider Nest, as some very helpful loot can be acquired there in Hardmode.

The following is a list of preparations you may wish to consider before summoning the Wall of Flesh:

  • Obtain maximum Health and Mana if you have not already done so.
  • Craft end of prehardmode equipment:

      • Armor: If you're doing a general playthrough, it's likely you'll want Molten armor, which provides 25 defense that is the best for basic survival in Hardmode. You may, however, have reason to prefer Shadow armor or Crimson armor, as they both provide more general stat bonuses and are easier to get: the Shadow armor gives (Old-gen console and 3DS versions) +21% melee speed (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions), +15% critical strike chance and increased movement speed, while the Crimson armor boosts damage by 6% along with increasing life regeneration. However, at this point in the game, setups for classes begin to diverge into different, distinct groups and you're going to have to be more specific with the type of damage you use. Therefore, you'll want to use the appropriate armor that corresponds with the weapons you have, as opposed to just taking whatever has the highest defense.
        • Melee: Melee players should have the Molten armor set, which costs 45 Hellstone Bars and provides 25 defense points (armors for Melee class will have the highest defense to survive more hits from enemies) as well as 17% increased melee damage, (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) 7% melee critical strike chance, and 7% melee speed.
        • Ranged: Rangers should have the Necro armor set, a post-Skeletron set that is crafted with 150 Bones and 135 Cobwebs. Despite having lower defense, it makes up for this by increasing ranged damage by 15% and a Set Bonus of (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) 10% increased ranged critical strike chance/(Old-gen console and 3DS versions) 20% chance not to consume ammo.
        • Magic: Magic users have three armor setups to choose from: the first is Jungle armor, which boosts maximum mana by (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) 80/(Old-gen console and 3DS versions) 60, reduces mana usage by 16%, boosts magic critical strike chance by (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) 12%/ (Old-gen console and 3DS versions) 9%, and (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) magic damage by 6%. It can be easily crafted after going to the Underground Jungle and looting its' contents and is made with 32 Jungle Spores, (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) 10/(Old-gen console and 3DS versions) 12 Stingers, and 2 Vines. The second option is the Meteor armor, which costs (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) 45/ (Old-gen console and 3DS versions) 60 Meteorite Bars (meaning that it can be crafted after a Meteorite falls), and increases magic damage by 21%. It also has a Set Bonus of the Space Gun, Gray Zapinator(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions), and Orange Zapinator(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) all costing 0 mana to use, so it is preferred if you are using any of those weapons. The third and last option consists of the Wizard Hat, Mystic Robe, and Meteor Leggings, which is a mix of multiple armor set pieces. The Wizard Hat is dropped by the rare Tim enemy underground, the Mystic Robe is sold by the Traveling Merchant for (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) 3 Gold 50 Silver/(Old-gen console version) 2 Gold, and the Meteor Leggings are crafted from 15 Meteorite Bars. This set increases magic damage by (Old-gen console version) 28%/ (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) 20%, magic critical strike chance by 16%, and reduces mana usage by 10%. This set generally provides the best magic damage while having the lowest defense.
        • Summoner: Summoners should use either Bee armor(Desktop, Console, Old-gen console and Mobile versions) or Obsidian armor(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) with both of which focusing on different elements of playing as a summoner: the Bee armor is made with 30 Bee Wax, meaning that crafting it requires defeating Queen Bee twice and it gives 2 minion slots and 23% summon damage, which is better for the players that prefer having an extra minion slot. The Obsidian armor, on the other hand, is focused on attacking via whips, giving 31% summon damage, 1 minion slot, 15% whip speed, and 30% whip range. It is crafted with 60 Obsidian, 30 Silk, and 20 Shadow Scales or Tissue Samples.
      • Weapons: At this point of the game, weapon classes begin to noticeably diverge. You should now start to focus on one or two classes, as it's much easier to progress when focusing on a few classes. Though many weapons are available at this stage, here are the ones you should have to make taking down the Wall of Flesh and handling Hardmode much easier.
        • Melee: The strongest sword available in pre-Hardmode is the Night's Edge, which is made by combining the Blade of Grass, Volcano, Muramasa, and either Light's Bane or Blood Butcherer (in Corruption and Crimson worlds respectively) at an Altar. This sword deals (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) 40/(Old-gen console and 3DS versions) 42 melee damage and will later be used to craft the Terra Blade, one of the most iconic and powerful swords in Hardmode. However, you may have reason to prefer some other swords. (Old-gen console and 3DS versions) The Blade of Grass and Volcano both have a greater range than the Night's Edge and inflict the Poisoned and On Fire! debuffs respectively. (Old-gen console and 3DS versions) The Night's Edge also lacks autoswing, while the Muramasa does have it. You're also going to want some melee weapons with larger range, as Hardmode enemies can easily overwhelm you if you're too close. The Flamarang (10 Hellstone Bars and an Enchanted Boomerang at an Iron/Lead Anvil) is the strongest pre-Hardmode boomerang, dealing (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) 49/(Old-gen console and 3DS versions) 37 damage, and can be very efficient when used strategically. The same applies to the Sunfury, the strongest flail, which is found in Shadow Chests and is extremely effective with large groups of enemies, dealing (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) 64/(Old-gen console and 3DS versions)33 damage. Both of these weapons have a chance of inflicting the On Fire! debuff, making them even more effective. The strongest yo-yos(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) at this stage are the Cascade and the Hive-Five. The Cascade has a 1 in 400 (0.25%) chance of being dropped by any enemy killed in the Underworld after Skeletron is defeated and inflicts the On Fire! debuff. The Hive-Five is crafted from 14 Bee Wax and spawns bees. They are both great weapons for stunlocking enemies or dealing with enemies in tight spaces. Finally, the strongest spear available is the Dark Lance, which can also be found in Shadow Chests.
        • Ranged: The ranger class, along with having multiple weapon choices, also has multiple ammunition choices. The best bow at this point is the Hellwing Bow, which is looted from Shadow Chests. Though it is inaccurate and only does 22 damage, it turns Wooden Arrows into piercing Hellwings (Flaming Bats). Additionally, it autofires and is very fast in doing so, making it especially efficient in the Wall of Flesh fight dealing with the Hungry or when fighting many enemies in a large range. The Molten Fury, crafted with 15 Hellstone Bars at an Iron/Lead Anvil, is more accurate, however it is slower at firing arrows. Although it cannot autofire, once again, it is accurate, does (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) 31/(Old-gen console and 3DS versions) 29 damage, and turns Wooden Arrows into Flaming Arrows when fired. Both bows are best used with Unholy/Jester Arrows, as they not only deal high damage, but also can pierce that can easily deal with large groups when pointed on one point. The Phoenix Blaster is the best pre-Hardmode gun, crafted with 10 Hellstone Bars and a Handgun at an Anvil. Though it does not autofire, it has a very fast use time, and therefore firing rate. It deals (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) 24/(Old-gen console and 3DS versions) 23 damage, and is very effective when paired with Meteor Shots against groups of enemies or the Party Bullets when used against a singular target. The Star Cannon (crafted with a Minishark, 20 Meteorite Bars, and 5 Fallen Stars) deals an insanely high 55 damage and can autofire. Though the Fallen Stars it uses as ammo can be difficult to collect, building a bridge in the sky may make the collecting process more simple and using them as ammo against both the Wall of Flesh can take it down.
        • Magic: Mages will begin to see their weapons heavily diversify, which makes Mage the most unique class at this point. There are various items the player can fight with; one of these is the Demon Scythe, which has a 1 in 35 (2.86%) chance of dropping from Demons and Voodoo Demons in the Underworld. Though it does not autofire, it is quick to use, pierces four enemies, and firing multiple Demon Sickles at a time can easily kill most enemies. The Book of Skulls is another great option for mages. It has a 36/343 (10.5%) / 1/3 (33.33%) chance of dropping from Skeletron and fires slow flying skulls that can pierce two enemies and, on the  Desktop version,  Console version, and  Mobile version, flies towards enemies. The way it "juggles" enemies makes it a formidable weapon through Hardmode. The Water Bolt can be found on the shelves of the Dungeon amongst other Books, and autofires multiple bolts of water that both pierce enemies and ricochet off blocks, making it especially effective in arenas and dense caves. Against the Wall of Flesh, the player can bounce them off the ceiling, allowing them to repeatedly pierce the Wall of Flesh's eyes and mouth. The Flamelash and Flower of Fire are both found in Shadow Chests: the former fires a ball of fire that can be controlled by the cursor, and, on the  Desktop version,  Console version, and  Mobile version, will home into enemies and, after hitting it, will home on and explode on contact with another enemy. Meanwhile, the latter fires a slow fireball that doesn't pierce but ricochets 4 times and deals (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) 48/ (Old-gen console and 3DS versions) damage. These are generally all the magic weapons you'll need – however, if you have the Meteor armor, the Space Gun fires very rapidly and doesn't cost any mana, meaning it could still remain effective.
        • Summoner: Finally, there are summoning weapons, which are generally the most limited at this stage of the game. There are really only two formidable choices. The first is the Hornet Staff, crafted with 14 Bee Wax, which inflicts 9 damage and shoots stingers at enemies, inflicting Poisoned for 4 to 7 seconds. Your second option is the Imp Staff, which is crafted with 17 Hellstone Bars and inflicts (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) 17/ (Old-gen console version) 21 damage and fires fireballs at enemies every 0.75 to 1.5 seconds, inflicting the On Fire! debuff for 3 to 6 seconds. Though the Imp Staff deals much more base damage and the debuff it inflicts is more damaging over time, its fire rate is a lot slower. Therefore, either summon is effective, though the latter may be preferred. (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) The Spinal Tap is the most powerful pre-hardmode whip in both terms of direct damage and summon tag damage, and is highly recommended. (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) The Snapthorn is another whip you could use, with benefits over the Spinal Tap being its chance of inflicting Poisoned onto enemies and its buff which provides an increase in attack speed compatible with other weapons.
      • Tools: The Molten Pickaxe is the highest tier pickaxe you can obtain at this stage, crafted with 20 Hellstone Bars. It can mine Cobalt and Palladium ore, the first tier Hardmode ores. However, on the  Old-gen console and 3DSversions, the Reaver Shark can be fished up in the Ocean with a 1 in 100 chance with 50% fishing power and has the same pickaxe power as the Molten Pickaxe, meaning it can be obtained early game rather than after defeating the Eater of Worlds/Brain of Cthulhu. The Molten Hamaxe, crafted with 15 Hellstone Bars, functions as both an axe and a hammer, and is the strongest hamaxe in pre-Hardmode.
      • Ensure you've obtained key accessories Many of these accessories are produced at the Tinkerer's Workshop, and the components will be much harder to get in Hardmode due to the much stronger enemies.
        • If at all possible, you should have created the following:
          • Frostspark Boots which allows flight, very fast running, and extra mobility on ice, alongside boosting movement speed on 8%. This accessory is especially necessary during boss fights. Lava Waders are another important mobility accessory underground, which provides the ability to walk on honey, lava, and water. It also grants immunity to fire blocks and 7 seconds of immunity when in lava. On the  Desktop version,  Console version, and  Mobile version, these two can be combined into the Terraspark Boots.
          • One of the Horseshoe Balloons, which provide increased jump height, double jump (the best double jump is from the Yellow Horseshoe Balloon, crafted with the Sandstorm in a Bottle), and immunity to fall damage. (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) The Bundle of Horseshoe Balloons, while being much more expensive than other Horseshoe Balloons, provides the quadruple jump ability of the Bundle of Balloons along with fall damage immunity.
          • Other useful equipment includes Lava Waders, Frog Leg, Jellyfish Diving Gear, Flying Carpet (if you have a Pyramid), Obsidian Shield, and Celestial Cuffs.
    • Ensure you've obtained key items. Many of these items are produced at the Tinkerer's Workshop, and the components will be much harder to get in Hardmode due to the much stronger enemies.
      • If at all possible, you should have created the following:
        • (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) Cell Phone, an informational accessory that displays current DPS, fishing power, location (horizontal and vertical), moon phase, nearest valuable items (such as chests, Life Crystals and Life Fruit, ore, and pots), player speed, rare creatures nearby, time, total amount of enemies nearby, total kills of the last enemy attacked, and weather. It also has the function of the Magic Mirror, returning the player home when they use it. The hardest parts of this accessory to obtain will likely be the Fisherman's Pocket Guide, Sextant, and Weather Radio, all rare rewards from the Angler. (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) Players on 1.4.4 can combine the Cell Phone with the Magic Conch and Demon Conch to make the Shellphone, providing the ability to teleport to the initial world spawn, the Underworld, and the Oceans in addition to the set spawn point.
        • (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) The Grand Design, a versatile wiring item that gives the player access to a menu easily controlling wiring. The player can place or remove actuators and any color of wire almost effortlessly, and the menu (accessed by right clicking) allows the player to easily change between wiring options. This makes it incredibly easy to create farms and other mechanisms requiring wiring.
      • Mining armor is also useful.
      • You will need a good multi-line Hook such as the Ivy Whip, Fish Hook, Skeletron Hand, or even the Slime Hook.
      • And some company: At least one minion as above, one or more Mounts, and a light pet. The Shadow Orb or Crimson Heart are basic and easy to obtain, while the Magic Lantern can help when exploring. A regular pet is optional and purely a cosmetic, but by now you should have some appealing choices.
      • Some items are meant for later: Feral Claws will start you on the path to the Fire Gauntlet, while a Bezoar and Nazar will be the first components of an Ankh Shield.
    • Ensure you have a sufficient stock of Potions.
      • You should have a farm for herbs (see Guide:Gardening)
      • Build secure fishing bases in all the major biomes, especially near your base. You might also want to build a lake of Honey for Honeyfins.
      • Build a bait farm to be able to fish sustainably.
    • Find Demon or Crimson Altars. Most Altars are found in the Corruption and Crimson respectively, so explore each Corruption or Crimson biome in the world. They need to be easily accessible when hardmode begins (further information in the Hardmode section).
    • Reforge Weapons and Accessories. You'll generally want Warding (+4 Defense), Menacing (+4% Damage), or Lucky (+4% Critical strike chance).
    • Build a surface Mushroom biome with a house for the Truffle NPC, as gathering the necessary materials will become much harder during hardmode.
    • Make sure you have 21 valid NPC houses, so you don't have to worry about building them later on. In fact, you should have rather more that that, but they shouldn't all be together. Have spare houses at all your bases, so that if a bunch of NPCs find themselves in the middle of the Corruption/Crimson, they have someplace to respawn.

    Here are some more open-ended ideas, many of which qualify as "big projects".

    • Creating quarantines. You probably want to limit the spread of the Corruption or Crimson, and the Hallow as well. Without preparation, the Hallow and your "evil" biome will quickly divvy up your world between them. There are a few reasons this is bad: These biomes are very hard when first entering Hardmode; NPCs will not live near Corruption or Crimson (which is a problem if your town gets converted); and there are some unique drops and resources only available from uninfected biomes. (Old-gen console and 3DS versions) You should particularly protect the Jungle and Ocean biomes in their natural state; in particular, if a Jungle or Mushroom Biome gets taken by evil, the conversion is irreversible. To block the spread of the biomes, you will need to dig tunnels and hellevators to chop up your world, restricting any infection to a relatively small area (or at least keeping it away from your more valuable areas). For more information on building quarantines, see Guide:Maintaining world purity.
    • Make the world accessible. Build a skybridge or a tunnel across your world, ideally with minecart tracks, to allow you to visit the new Hardmode biomes relatively safely and quickly. (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) The Magic Conch and Demon Conch allow you to quickly teleport to the ocean shores and the center of the underworld.
    • Rebuild your base. This is a good time to reconsider your main base(s) and rebuild them to something that has space for all your crafting stations and chests, with extra for growth, and houses for convenient access to favored NPCs.
    • Farming money. Some vendors sell new, but expensive items in Hardmode and reforging Hardmode weapons is extremely expensive. You may want to farm a few platinum if you would like to enter hardmode fairly prepared. For more information on farming money, see Guide:Making money.
    • Rearrange the Landscape. Is there some area that's inconvenient to you? Change it! Want a lake or a mountain someplace? You can do it now.

    Activating Hardmode

    Once the player is ready to move on to the next phase of their world, Hardmode, then they will have to head to the underworld and fight the Wall of Flesh. Once the player defeats this boss, they will receive weapons and accessories to boost their survivability in early Hardmode. The player will also receive a message saying, "The ancient spirits of light and dark have been released." This indicates that the world has transitioned into hardmode.
sections.content_text: At this point you have no deadlines or threats looming over you. You should be more-or-less the master of all you survey, and you have a wide variety of resources available. This is a good time to do large projects like arenas, bases, or farms, though you should keep in mind that depending on location, your base or arena might end up in an infected biome . You'll also need to collect some materials that will be needed in Hardmode , as farming is a lot easier in pre-Hardmode . You should also locate and construct a safe path to a Spider Nest , as some very helpful loot can be acquired there in Hardmode. One of the Horseshoe Balloons , which provide increased jump height, double jump (the best double jump is from the Yellow Horseshoe Balloon , crafted with the Sandstorm in a Bottle ), and immunity to fall damage. Other useful equipment includes Lava Waders , Frog Leg , Jellyfish Diving Gear , Flying Carpet (if you have a Pyramid ), Obsidian Shield , and Celestial Cuffs . Ensure you've obtained key items . Many of these items are produced at the Tinkerer's Workshop , and the components will be much harder to get in Hardmode due to the much stronger enemies. If at all possible, you should have created the following: (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) Cell Phone , an informational accessory that displays current DPS , fishing power , location ( horizontal and vertical ), moon phase , nearest valuable items (such as chests , Life Crystals and Life Fruit , ore, and pots ), player speed , rare creatures nearby , time , total amount of enemies nearby , total kills of the last enemy attacked , and weather . It also has the function of the Magic Mirror , returning the player home when they use it. The hardest parts of this accessory to obtain will likely be the Fisherman's Pocket Guide, Sextant, and Weather Radio, all rare rewards from the Angler . (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) Players on 1.4.4 can combine the Cell Phone with the Magic Conch and Demon Conch to make the Shellphone , providing the ability to teleport to the initial world spawn, the Underworld, and the Oceans in addition to the set spawn point. (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) The Grand Design , a versatile wiring item that gives the player access to a menu easily controlling wiring. The player can place or remove actuators and any color of wire almost effortlessly, and the menu (accessed by right clicking) allows the player to easily change between wiring options. This makes it incredibly easy to create farms and other mechanisms requiring wiring. Mining armor is also useful. You will need a good multi-line Hook such as the Ivy Whip , Fish Hook , Skeletron Hand , or even the Slime Hook . And some company: At least one minion as above, one or more Mounts , and a light pet . The Shadow Orb or Crimson Heart are basic and easy to obtain, while the Magic Lantern can help when exploring. A regular pet is optional and purely a cosmetic, but by now you should have some appealing choices. Some items are meant for later: Feral Claws will start you on the path to the Fire Gauntlet , while a Bezoar and Nazar will be the first components of an Ankh Shield . Ensure you have a sufficient stock of Potions . You should have a farm for herbs (see Guide:Gardening ) Build secure fishing bases in all the major biomes, especially near your base. You might also want to build a lake of Honey for Honeyfins . Build a bait farm to be able to fish sustainably. Find Demon or Crimson Altars . Most Altars are found in the Corruption and Crimson respectively, so explore each Corruption or Crimson biome in the world. They need to be easily accessible when hardmode begins (further information in the Hardmode section). Reforge Weapons and Accessories . You'll generally want Warding (+4 Defense), Menacing (+4% Damage), or Lucky (+4% Critical strike chance). Build a surface Mushroom biome with a house for the Truffle NPC , as gathering the necessary materials will become much harder during hardmode. Make sure you have 21 valid NPC houses , so you don't have to worry about building them later on. In fact, you should have rather more that that, but they shouldn't all be together. Have spare houses at all your bases, so that if a bunch of NPCs find themselves in the middle of the Corruption/Crimson, they have someplace to respawn. Here are some more open-ended ideas, many of which qualify as "big projects". Creating quarantines . You probably want to limit the spread of the Corruption or Crimson, and the Hallow as well. Without preparation, the Hallow and your "evil" biome will quickly divvy up your world between them. There are a few reasons this is bad: These biomes are very hard when first entering Hardmode; NPCs will not live near Corruption or Crimson (which is a problem if your town gets converted); and there are some unique drops and resources only available from uninfected biomes. (Old-gen console and 3DS versions) You should particularly protect the Jungle and Ocean biomes in their natural state; in particular, if a Jungle or Mushroom Biome gets taken by evil, the conversion is irreversible. To block the spread of the biomes, you will need to dig tunnels and hellevators to chop up your world, restricting any infection to a relatively small area (or at least keeping it away from your more valuable areas). For more information on building quarantines, see Guide:Maintaining world purity . Make the world accessible. Build a skybridge or a tunnel across your world, ideally with minecart tracks , to allow you to visit the new Hardmode biomes relatively safely and quickly. (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) The Magic Conch and Demon Conch allow you to quickly teleport to the ocean shores and the center of the underworld. Rebuild your base. This is a good time to reconsider your main base(s) and rebuild them to something that has space for all your crafting stations and chests, with extra for growth, and houses for convenient access to favored NPCs. Farming money . Some vendors sell new, but expensive items in Hardmode and reforging Hardmode weapons is extremely expensive. You may want to farm a few platinum if you would like to enter hardmode fairly prepared. For more information on farming money, see Guide:Making money . Rearrange the Landscape. Is there some area that's inconvenient to you? Change it! Want a lake or a mountain someplace? You can do it now. Activating Hardmode Once the player is ready to move on to the next phase of their world, Hardmode, then they will have to head to the underworld and fight the Wall of Flesh. Once the player defeats this boss, they will receive weapons and accessories to boost their survivability in early Hardmode. The player will also receive a message saying, "The ancient spirits of light and dark have been released." This indicates that the world has transitioned into hardmode.

sections.title: Overview
sections.content_html:
The Witcher 3: Wild Hunt CD PROJEKT RED witcher Geralt of Rivia The Witcher 2: Assassins of Kings

Unlike the previous games, The Witcher 3 is set in a multi-region open world, featuring over 100 hours of content. Several early articles mentioned that the developers planned to have an open world similar to that of Skyrim, but 20% larger. The developers were quick to point out that while there was much to appreciate in Bethesda's open world concept, they were also making an effort not to repeat what they perceived as the flaws in-game. As with earlier games, the consequences of Geralt's actions will impact how the narrative progresses. The game has been built using the new REDengine 3 and was designed with player feedback from fans of previous Witcher games in mind.

For fans of the series, the online event "Killing Monsters", a weekly giveaway of wallpapers and audio files that ran from 10 June 2013 to 14 August 2013, culminated in the release of the "Killing Monsters" cinematic trailer.

On 14 May 2015, CD PROJEKT RED (working with Digic Pictures) released a pre-launch short story trailer titled "A Night to Remember".

During Gamescom Opening Night Live 2026, it was announced the game was getting a remaster due to be released on September 29, 2026 and would be a free upgrade to those who already owned the game. At the same time, it was also revealed that the first two expansions (Hearts of Stone and Blood and Wine) were being made available for free to all those who owned the base game.

sections.title: Later releases
sections.content_html:
At E3 2019, a port for Nintendo Switch got announced. It was developed in collaboration with Saber Interactive and released on October 15, 2019 as a Complete Edition with both expansions and 16 DLCs on a 32-GB cartridge (or as a single download, respectively). On January 28th of 2021, CDPR announced that the base game and the expansions would be made available separately, and that the Complete Edition would eventually get phased out. As of August 2025, the digital Complete Edition is still available alongside the base game and its season pass (consisting of the also separately available expansions). For the physical version, a new release with only the base game got released on November 1st, 2021, seemingly replacing the Complete Edition. This new physical edition is not being mentioned on Nintendo's or CDPR's game pages.

On September 4, 2020, it was announced that the game and its expansions would be getting a next-generation upgrade and would be released as a standalone purchase for the next-generation consoles (Xbox Series X and PlayStation 5) as well as PC. A free update would be given out to those who already own the game on the PC, Xbox One, and PlayStation 4. While it was originally expected to be released in 2021 it was later announced that the next-generation update had been delayed to 2022 before CDPR announced it'd be released on December 14, 2022.

On November 15, 2023, CD PROJEKT RED announced a mod editor was being created for the game to be released in 2024 and would be available for free for all owners of The Witcher 3: Wild Hunt on PC. In May 2024, they released a new version of REDkit for the game.

sections.title: Story
sections.content_html:
For the main article, see The Witcher 3 storyline.

The world is in chaos. The air is thick with tension and the smoke of burnt villages. The fearsome Empire of Nilfgaard has struck again, ravaging the helpless Northern Kingdoms. The once mighty who tried to use Geralt for their own gain are now gone. In these uncertain times, no one can say what fortune holds in store, who will bring peace to the world and who will cause it only misery. But a force darker and deadlier emerges.

The petty men and women commanding tin-plated armies fail to understand that their conflict is child's play compared to the Wild Hunt, the otherworldly threat which now looms. These ghastly spectral riders have for ages plagued humankind, bringing misery to the world. This time the Wild Hunt seeks one person in particular: the one individual Destiny itself bestowed upon Geralt, the one soul Geralt considers kin.

sections.title: Features
sections.content_html:
General

  • The grand finale to Geralt's story
  • A standalone adventure easily accessible to new players
  • Meaningful choices with consequences that change the story and the game world
  • Quests and main story threads that can be resolved in any order or completed in parallel
  • Unforgettable quests deeply linked with the core storyline and designed with care to draw players in
  • A breathtaking cinematic introduction illustrating the game background
  • Unique atmosphere, memorable characters, and gritty dialogue

Open world

  • A vast open world - 35 times larger than that in The Witcher 2
  • Multiple ecosystems and cultures that players can move between at will
  • Regions with different inspirations and deep cultural references, each with a distinct feel
  • Free exploration unspoiled by loading times

Living world

  • A world shaped by the player's decisions, but which, left to itself, goes on living
  • A realistic day and night cycle
  • A dynamic weather system
  • A living economy: The new in-game economy system varies the price of goods based on surrounding conditions or their place of origin relative to Geralt's current whereabouts in the world: the price of fish might differ depending on distance from water, and a village lying on a trade route for trappers and hunters might have many tanneries and leather workers, affecting the price of crafting components and armor.
  • A unique, deep, consistent and expansive game world based on that described by Andrzej Sapkowski

Combat

  • Combat complexity based on a variety of actions at the player's disposal, not on correct attack sequencing
  • A Witcher Senses system bringing new tactical depth to combat
  • Monsters, each with their own lore, posing unique hunting challenges and responding to changes in the environment

RPG

  • A tutorial built into the game, allowing players to dive into the world of the Witcher with ease
  • Involving investigations and rewarding hunts through the Witcher Senses mechanic
  • A completely rewritten RPG mechanic allowing players to see the influence of statistics on gameplay
  • An expanded Sign casting system: each of the 5 Signs has two different modes of use, creating even more possibilities in combat and challenging players to use magic in creative ways
  • A highly-intuitive Alchemy system
  • An expanded character development system
  • Advanced Crafting mechanics

Visuals

  • Fully dynamic light and shadow effects throughout the game world, generating superior atmosphere and ambiance
  • Detailed, realistic locations through a significant increase in polygon numbers
  • A deep role-playing experience through visually attractive, film-like presentation

sections.title: Free downloadable content
sections.content_html: As CD PROJEKT RED, we strongly believe this is not the way it should work and, with The Witcher 3: Wild Hunt​​​, we have decided to do it differently. Cutting to the chase, everyone who buys Wild Hunt will receive 16 specially prepared DLCs absolutely for free, regardless of platform. You don't have to preorder, you don't have to buy any special edition to get them — if you own a copy of Wild Hunt, they're yours. This is our way of saying thank you for buying our game.

sections.title: Expansions
sections.content_html:
On April 7, 2015, CD PROJEKT RED announced two major expansions for The Witcher 3: Wild Hunt, entitled Hearts of Stone and Blood and Wine. CD PROJEKT RED said that both expansion packs included new enemies, characters, and gear. Players would also be reunited with some "dearly missed" characters from the series. Hearts of Stone was released on October 13, 2015, and Blood and Wine on May 31, 2016, both are available on all three major platforms. Players can purchase both expansions at once by getting the Expansion Pass, now on sale through several retailers.

On August 30, 2016, a Game of the Year edition (for PC) and Complete edition (for consoles) was released, containing the base game, both expansions, and all downloadable content.

On May 27, 2026, CD PROJEKT RED announced it was working with Fool's Theory on a third expansion, Songs of the Past. It's expected to launch sometime in 2027 for PlayStation 5, Xbox Series X|S, and PC.

Hearts of Stone expansion

Hearts of Stone is a major expansion that adds over ten hours of additional content. Geralt will adventure into the wilds of No Man's Land and the nooks and alleys of Oxenfurt, where he will try to complete a contract from the mysterious Man of Glass. Caught in a thick tangle of deceit, Geralt will need all his cunning and strength to solve the mystery and emerge unscathed.

Blood and Wine expansion

Blood and Wine is a major expansion that adds over twenty hours of additional content. A tale that will introduce the all-new in-game region of Toussaint, Blood and Wine will take Geralt to a land untainted by war, where an atmosphere of carefree indulgence and knightly ritual masks an ancient and bloody secret.
